 Part 1 READING PASSAGE 1 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1-13 , which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. 

 How the mind ages
 The way mental function changes is largely determined by three factors-mental lifestyle, the impact of chronic disease and flexibility of the mind. 
 Experiments have shown that younger monkeys consistently outperform their older colleagues on memory tests. Formerly, psychologists concluded that memory and other mental functions in humans deteriorate over time because of changes in the brain. Thus mental decline after young adulthood appeared inevitable. The truth, however, is not quite so simple.
 Stanley Rapoport at the National Institute of Health in the United States measured the flow of blood in the brains of old and young people as they completed different tasks. Since blood flow reflects neural activity. Rapoport could compare which networks of neurons were the same, the neural networks they used were significantly different. The older subjects used different internal strategies to accomplish comparable results at the same time,'Rapoport says. At the Georgia Institute of Technology, psychologist Timothy Salthouse compared a group of fast and accurate typists of college age with another group in their 60s. Both groups typed 60 words a minute. The older typists, it turned out, achieved their speed with cunning little strategies that made them more efficient than their younger counterparts. They made fewer finger shifts, gaining a fraction of a second here and there. They also read ahead in the test. The neural networks involved in typing appear to have been reshaped to compensate for losses in motor skills or other age changes.
 In fact, there's evidence that deterioration in mental functions can actually be reversed. Neuropsychologist Marion Diamond at the University of California has shown that mental activity maks neurons sprout new dendrites* which establish connections with other neurons. The dendrites shrink when the mind is idle. For example,'when a rat is kept in isolation, the animal's brain shrinks, but if we put that rat with other rats in a large cage and give them an assortment of toys, we can show, after four days, significant differences in its brain.'says Diamond. After a month in the enriched surroundings, the whole cerebral cortex has expanded, as has its blood supply.'But even in the enriched surroundings, rats get bored unless the toys are varied. Animals are just like we are. They need stimulation,'says Diamond. A busy mental lifestyle keeps the human mind fit, says Warner Schaie of Penn State University. ‘People who regularly participate in challenging tasks retain their intellectual abilities better than mental couch potatoes.'
 In his studies, Schaie detected a decline in mental function among individuals who underwent lengthy stays in hospital for chronic illness. He postulated it might be due to the mental passivity encouraged by hospital routine.
 One of the most profoundly important mental functions is memory. Memory exists in more than one form, what we call knowledge- facts- is what psychologists such as Harry Bahrick of Ohio Wesleyan University call semantic memory. Events, conversations and occurrences in time and space, on the other hand, make up episodic memory. It's true that episodic memory begins to decline when most people are in their 50s, but it's never perfect at any age.
 Probing the longevity of knowledge, Bahrick tested 1,000 high school graduates to see how well they remembered the school subject algebra. Some had completed the course a month before, other 50 years earlier. Surprisingly, he found that a person's grasp of algebra did not depend on how long ago he'd taken the course. The determining factor was the duration of instruction. Those who had spent only a few months learning algebra forgot most of it within two or three years while others who had been instructed for longer remembered better. According to Bahrick,'the long-term residue of knowledge remains stable over the decades, independent of the age of the person and the memory.'
 Perhaps even more important than the ability to remember is the ability to manage memory- a mental function known as metamemory.'You could say metamemory is a byproduct of going to school,'says psychologist Robert Kail of Purdue University,'The question-and-answer process,especially exam taking, helps children learn and teaches them how their memory functions.This may be one reason why the better educated a person is, the more likely they are to perform well in many aspects of life and in psychological assessments: A group of adult novice chess players were compared with a group of child experts at the game. But when asked to remember the patterns of chess pieces arranged on a board, the children won.' Because they'd played a lot of chess, their knowledge of chess was better organized than that of the adults, and their existing knowledge of chess served as a framework for new memory,'explains Kail. Cognitive style, another factor in maintaining mental function, is what Schaie calls the ability to adapt and roll with life's punches.'He measured mental flexibility with questions and tests requiring people to carry out in an offbeat way an everyday activity they had done millions of times. One example was asking people to copy a paragraph substituting uppercase letters for lowercase ones. These tests seem silly, but flexible-minded people manage to complete them,'says Schaie. The rigid person responds with tension instead and performs poorly. Those who score highly on tests of cognition at an advanced age are those who tested high in mental flexibility at middle age'.
 On a more optimistic note, one mental resource that only improves with time is specialized knowledge. Crystallised intelligence about one's occupation apparently does not decline at all until at least age 75. Vocabulary is another such specialized form of knowledge. Research clearly shows that vocabulary develops with time. Retired teachers and journalists consistently score higher on tests of vocabulary and general information than college students.

 Part 2 READING PASSAGE 2 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26 , which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. 

 Ensuring our future food supply
 Climate change and new diseases threaten the limited varieties of seeds we depend on for food. Luckily, we still have many of the seeds used in the past-but we must take steps to save them.
 Six miles outside the town of Decorah, Iowa in the USA, an 890-acre stretch of rolling fields and woods called Heritage Farm is letting its crops go to seed. Everything about Heritage Farm is in stark contrast to the surrounding acres of intensively farmed fields of corn and soybean that are typical of modern agriculture. Heritage Farm is devoted to collecting rather than growing seeds. It is home to the Seed Savers Exchange, one of the largest non government-owned seed banks in the United States.
 In 1975 Diane Ott Whealy was given the seedlings of two plant varieties that her great grandfather had brought to America from Bavaria in 1870: Grandpa Ott’s morning glory and his German Pink tomato. Wanting to preserve similar traditional varieties, known as heirloom plants, Diane and her husband, Kent, decided to establish a place where the seeds of the past could be kept and traded. The exchange now has more than 13,000 members, and the many thousands of heirloom varieties they have donated are kept in its walk-in coolers, freezers, and root cellars the seeds of many thousands of heirloom varieties and, as you walk around an old red barn that is covered in Grandpa Ott’s beautiful morning glory blossoms, you come across the different vegetables, herbs, and flowers they have planted there.
 "Each year our members list their seeds in this,"Diane Ott Whealy says, handing over a copy of the Seed Savers Exchange 2010 Yearbook. It is as thick as a big-city telephone directory, with page after page of exotic beans, garlic, potatoes, peppers, apples, pears, and plums-each with its own name and personal history .For example, there’s an Estonian Yellow Cherry tomato, which was brought to the seed bank by “an elderly Russian lady” who lived in Tallinn, and a Persian Star garlic from “a bazaar in Samarkand.”There’s also a bean donated by archaeologists searching for pygmy elephant fossils in New Mexico.
 Heirloom vegetables have become fashionable in the United States and Europe over the past decade, prized by a food movement that emphasizes eating locally and preserving the flavor and uniqueness of heirloom varieties. Found mostly in farmers' markets and boutique groceries, heirloom varieties have been squeezed out of supermarkets in favor of modern single-variety fruits and vegetables bred to ship well and have a uniform appearance, not to enhance flavor. But the movement to preserve heirloom varieties goes way beyond the current interest in North America and Europe in tasty, locally grown food. It’s also a campaign to protect the world’s future food supply.Most people in the well-fed world give little thought to where their food comes from or how it’s grown. They wander through well-stocked supermarkets without realizing that there may be problem ahead.We’ve been hearing for some time about the loss of flora and fauna in our rainforests.Very little,by contrast,is being said or done about the parallel decline in the diversity of the foods we eat.
 Food variety extinction is happening all over the world - and it's happening fast. In the United States an estimated 90 percent of historic fruit and vegetable varieties are no longer grown. Of the 7,000 different apple varieties that were grown in the 1800s, fewer than a hundred remain. In the Philippines thousands of varieties of rice once thrived; now only about a hundred are grown there. In China 90 percent of the wheat varieties cultivated just a hundred years ago have disappeared. Experts estimate that in total we have lost more than 50 percent of the world's food varieties over the past century.
 Why is this a problem? Because if disease or future climate change affects one of the handful of plants we've come to depend on to feed our growing planet, we might desperately need one of those varieties we've let become extinct. The loss of the world's cereal diversity is a particular cause for concern. A fungus called Ug99, which was first identified in Uganda in 1999, is spreading across the world's wheat crops. From Uganda it moved to Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, and Yemen. By 2007 it had jumped the Persian Gulf into Iran. Scientists predict that the fungus will soon make its way into India and Pakistan, then spread to Russia and China, and eventually the USA.
 Roughly 90 percent of the world's wheat has no defense against this particular fungus. If it reached the USA, an estimated one billion dollars' worth of crops would be at risk. Scientists believe that in Asia and Africa alone, the portion currently in danger could leave one billion people without their primary food source. A famine with significant humanitarian consequences could follow, according to Rick Ward of Cornell University.
 The population of the world is expected to reach nine billion by 2045. Some experts say we’ll need to double our food production to keep up with this growth. Given the added challenge of climate change and disease, it is becoming ever more urgent to find ways to increase food yield. The world has become increasingly dependent upon a technology-driven, one-size-fits-all approach to food supply. Yet the best hope for securing our food's future may depend on our ability to preserve the locally cultivated foods of the past.

 Part 3 READING PASSAGE 3 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40 , which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. 

 The fluoridation controversy
 The long-standing debate about whether to fluoridate our drinking water continues Fluoridation is the addition of fluorine to public water supplies with the aim of reducing tooth decay. The fluorine, when mixed with water, becomes fluoride and the desired concentration of fluoride in public water is approximately one part per million, depending on the regional temperature and hence the amount of water people are likely to drink. Many studies, such as those by McClure in 1970 through to Burt in 1983, have shown that when children drink fluoridated water, their average rate of tooth decay seems greatly reduced. A typical figure claimed is 50 percent reduction. This apparently enormous benefit for children's teeth is the major argument in favor of fluoridation.
 Three main grounds for opposition to fluoridation have been expressed. First, opponents claim the benefits are exaggerated or not established. Second, there are claims of health risks to pans of the population, for example, allergic reactions. It is also accepted that high levels of fluoride can cause discoloration of otherwise healthy teeth. Proponents do not consider this to be a problem in such small concentrations, whereas opponents disagree - especially because some people drink more water and obtain much more than the standard 1 milligram of fluoride per day. Third, fluoridation is thought to be an infringement on individual rights because it is compulsory medication of all members of a community.
 An understanding of the fluoridation issue has important implications. If, according to the experts, fluoridation is unquestionably a beneficial and non-hazardous measure, then the wisdom of allowing the public to vote on, and reject it must be questioned.
 Almost all studies that have been done have assumed that the scientific aspects of the controversy are unproblematic, and they have excluded science from sociological examination. The traditional view is that science is a special kind of knowledge, which is established through scientific methods and objectively applied by members of a scientific community. However, in recent years there has been a major challenge to this picture by a sociology of science that shows how scientific knowledge is socially negotiated, and inevitably linked to the values of the relevant parties, both scientists and nonscientists. These challengers do not see scientific knowledge as exempt from social inquiry.
 Kuhn (1970) argued that scientific knowledge does not always develop as an orderly process, but is characterized by periodic revolutions. in which the methods of study and the assessment criteria change in a fragmented way. According to Kuhn, the shift from one scientific way of thinking to another is not made solely on the basis of clear rules of formal scientific practice, but can include social factors, though Kuhn has never developed a full analysis of what these might be. Collins (1975) took this concept further when he asserted that the outcome of experiments was not something whose meaning could be immediately comprehended, but rather something for interpretation, discussion between scientists, and reinterpretation in the light of other experiments.
 One interpretation of this analysis of science is that traditional distinctions between facts and theories, and between scientific knowledge and values, can no longer be justified. Because social processes are involved at all stages of the creation, evaluation, and establishing of scientific knowledge, social values may also be involved.
 In the same way as many scientists who study fluoridation have overlooked social values, sociologists have also downplayed an important part of the debate by ignoring the number of eminent scientists who have questioned aspects of fluoridation. An example is the study by Sutton in 1960, which analyzed the classic North American studies of the effect of fluoridation on tooth decay, and found that each showed significant methodological shortcomings. Sutton's detailed study throws doubt as to the extent of reductions in tooth decay from fluoridation. Yet Sutton's book is not cited in a single analysis of the fluoridation issue by any sociologist. In a situation of some scientific uncertainty, differences in values are highlighted. A supporter of fluoridation might argue. The evidence for the benefits of fluoridation is quite substantial, while the evidence for harm is limited and dubious. I think the likely benefits outweigh the possible dangers; hence I support fluoridation because it is the cheapest and easiest way to make sure every child reaps the benefits. An opponent might argue, 'Though the evidence for the benefits of fluoridation is substantial, there is some doubt about it. Since fluoridation is not necessary for good teeth, we should forego the benefits if there is some slight chance of harm. Some scientists claim that a small percentage of the population could be harmed by fluoride. Therefore I oppose fluoridation of water supplies and favor the voluntary use of fluoride tablets by those who want to take them.'
 Both arguments consider the scientific evidence concerning fluoridation, but differ in their assessments of the social benefits and costs. This difference is not between rationality and irrationality but is a legitimate difference in values, for example, the positive value placed on good teeth, the negative value placed on possible health risks, and the social benefits or costs of compulsory or voluntary intake of fluorides.
 From the sociological point of view, opposition to fluoridation is not necessarily irrational. Rather, claims to rationality and to scientific authority are better seen as part of a strategy to promote fluoridation than as incontrovertible statements of fact. Second, social values are likely to be bound up in any decision about fluoridation, so this is not an issue on which declarations by scientific experts ought to be considered the final word.

 Part 2 

 Questions 14-20 

 Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage? In boxes 14-20 on your answer sheet, write.

Các cấu trúc ngữ pháp cao cấp khuyên dùng để đạt Band 9.0 (Grammatical Range and Accuracy):
1. Mệnh đề nhượng bộ lồng hợp phức (Complex Concession): 'While the merits of industrialized agriculture are undeniable, the preservation of heirloom seeds is equally imperative.'
2. Đảo ngữ với trạng từ phủ định hoặc giới hạn (Inversion): 'Not only does monoculture threaten ecological resilience, but it also leaves global food systems vulnerable to catastrophic blights.'
3. Câu điều kiện loại 3 hoặc câu điều kiện hỗn hợp giả định (Mixed/Past Conditionals): 'Had ancestral farmers not maintained crop diversity, contemporary society would lack the genetic baseline required to withstand modern plant diseases.'
4. Mệnh đề quan hệ rút gọn dạng phân từ (Reduced Relative Clauses): 'Food production driven by a one-size-fits-all approach often overlooks local ecological balances.'
5. Danh từ hóa hành động (Nominalization) làm chủ ngữ phức: 'The systematic eradication of traditional crop variations for the sake of uniform appearance constitutes a major threat.'

Bước 1: Phân tích đề bài (Task Analysis)
- Chủ đề (Topic): Xu hướng độc canh, tối ưu hóa vận chuyển và sản lượng của nông nghiệp hiện đại làm biến mất các giống cây truyền thống, đặt ra cuộc tranh luận giữa bảo tồn quá khứ và phát triển công nghệ tương lai.
- Loại câu hỏi (Question Type): Discuss both views and give your opinion (Thảo luận cả 2 quan điểm và đưa ra ý kiến cá nhân).
- Yêu cầu cốt lõi: Phải phân tích sâu sắc cả hai khía cạnh: Tại sao việc bảo tồn giống cũ lại quan trọng, và tại sao công nghệ/độc canh hiện đại lại được coi là giải pháp thiết yếu cho dân số bùng nổ. Cuối cùng, người viết phải thể hiện rõ ràng lập trường của mình.

Bước 2: Xác định lập trường cá nhân (Personal Position)
- Hướng tiếp cận Band 9.0: Đứng về phía dung hòa mang tính chiến lược nhưng nghiêng về bảo tồn đa dạng sinh học. Công nghệ hiện đại giải quyết bài toán sản lượng ngắn hạn, nhưng việc bảo tồn các giống cổ truyền (heirloom varieties) chính là 'bảo hiểm sinh học' bắt buộc phải có để đối phó với biến đổi khí hậu và dịch bệnh đột biến trong tương lai.
fields.ideas:
Dàn ý bài viết chi tiết:

1. Introduction:
- Paraphrase đề bài: Sự trỗi dậy của nông nghiệp công nghiệp hóa làm suy giảm đa dạng sinh học lương thực, dẫn đến các quan điểm trái chiều giữa việc duy trì phương pháp canh tác truyền thống và áp dụng tối đa công nghệ hiện đại.
- Thesis Statement: Thừa nhận vai trò của công nghệ trong việc cứu đói tạm thời, nhưng khẳng định việc bảo tồn đa dạng di truyền của các giống cây cổ truyền mới là chìa khóa sống còn cho an ninh lương thực lâu dài.

2. Body 1: View 1 - Vai trò của nông nghiệp công nghệ hiện đại (Yield & Efficiency):
- Lập luận: Dân số thế giới dự kiến đạt 9 tỷ người, đòi hỏi sản lượng phải tăng gấp đôi. Nông nghiệp công nghiệp hóa với các giống đơn nhất (single-variety) giúp tối ưu hóa dây chuyền, thu hoạch đồng bộ, chịu được vận chuyển đường dài mà không hỏng.
- Hệ quả: Giúp hạ giá thành lương thực, cung ứng quy mô lớn cho các siêu thị đô thị toàn cầu.

3. Body 2: View 2 - Tầm quan trọng của việc bảo tồn giống cây truyền thống (Resilience & Insurance):
- Lập luận: Tính đồng nhất về mặt di truyền của nông nghiệp hiện đại là một quả bom nổ chậm. Nếu một loại nấm bệnh mới (ví dụ như chủng Ug99 tấn công lúa mì) xuất hiện, 90% cây trồng sẽ không có khả năng phòng ngự, dẫn đến nạn đói hàng loạt.
- Hệ quả: Các giống cây cổ truyền của quá khứ ẩn chứa các gen kháng bệnh tự nhiên và khả năng chịu hạn do biến đổi khí hậu. Bảo tồn chúng chính là bảo vệ kho báu di truyền để lai tạo khi khủng hoảng xảy ra.

4. Conclusion:
- Tóm tắt lại cả hai mặt và khẳng định: Sự phát triển công nghệ không được phép đánh đổi bằng việc xóa sổ các giống loài cũ. Một hệ thống nông nghiệp tương lai bền vững phải là sự kết hợp giữa kỹ thuật canh tác hiện đại và việc lưu trữ nghiêm ngặt các nguồn gen cổ truyền.
fields.sample:
The industrialization of contemporary agriculture has catalysed a shift towards monoculture, where single-variety crops are engineered for uniform appearance and maximum transportability. While a segment of society argues that high-tech, industrialized farming is the sole mechanism capable of feeding an exploding global population, others contend that preserving heirloom and locally cultivated crops is vital to securing humankind's future food supply. This essay will examine both perspectives before arguing that genetic preservation acts as an indispensable insurance policy against ecological catastrophe, making it a priority over mere technological homogeneity.

On the one hand, the arguments supporting technology-driven, large-scale agriculture are grounded in immediate logistical necessity. With the global population projected to soar to unprecedented heights, traditional farming methods are often deemed insufficient to meet the surging demand for food. Modern agribusiness addresses this challenge by selecting and mass-producing high-yielding varieties that exhibit physical resilience during long-distance shipping, thereby minimizing post-harvest waste. Consequently, supermarkets remain consistently well-stocked, and food prices are kept affordable for urban populations. From an economic and humanitarian standpoint, this technological approach provides a predictable and scalable response to global food insecurity, ensuring that basic caloric requirements are fulfilled efficiently.

However, this focus on efficiency introduces a precarious systemic vulnerability. The primary danger of replacing thousands of local crop varieties with a handful of standardized crops is the erasure of genetic diversity. Should a highly virulent pathogen or an abrupt climatic shift target one of these few relied-upon varieties, the consequences would be catastrophic. For instance, the spread of the Ug99 fungus poses an existential threat to global wheat production because the vast majority of commercial crops possess no innate defense against it. Preserving ancient, locally cultivated varieties provides humanity with a critical genetic repository. These historical crops have survived centuries of environmental fluctuations and pest outbreaks, harboring resilient traits that modern scientists can utilize to breed disease-resistant hybrids. 

In conclusion, although technological advancements in farming offer necessary high yields to sustain the current population, they should not be pursued at the expense of agricultural heritage. In my opinion, the survival of humanity depends not on choosing technology over tradition, but on leveraging modern science to systematically safeguard and study the rich agricultural varieties of the past, thereby ensuring a resilient food infrastructure for generations to come.
fields.solution:
Phân tích chiến lược giải bài Band 9.0:

1. Về Task Achievement:
- Bài viết hoàn thành xuất sắc việc thảo luận cân bằng cả hai quan điểm ('Discuss both views') ở Body 1 và Body 2.
- Lập trường cá nhân được lồng ghép tinh tế nhưng rõ ràng ngay từ Introduction (genetic preservation acts as an indispensable insurance policy), tiếp tục khẳng định ở Body 2 và chốt lại mạnh mẽ ở Conclusion.
- Sử dụng chất liệu học thuật từ chính chủ đề của bài đọc (như dịch nấm lúa mì Ug99) để làm ví dụ thực tế cực kỳ đắt giá, giúp bài viết có chiều sâu chuyên môn vượt bậc.

2. Về Coherence and Cohesion:
- Các ý tưởng chuyển tiếp rất mượt mà. Giữa Body 1 (ca ngợi công nghệ) và Body 2 (nói về rủi ro của công nghệ) được kết nối bằng một câu chuyển ý đầy tương phản: 'However, this focus on efficiency introduces a precarious systemic vulnerability.'
- Sử dụng phân đoạn chuẩn mực, mỗi đoạn gánh vác một nhiệm vụ học thuật rõ ràng.

3. Về Lexical Resource:
- Từ vựng đạt độ chính xác tuyệt đối về ngữ cảnh (collocations hoàn hảo): 'catalysed a shift', 'technological homogeneity', 'precarious systemic vulnerability', 'virulent pathogen', 'existential threat', 'genetic repository', 'disease-resistant hybrids'.

4. Mẹo nâng band nhanh cho học viên:
Khi gặp dạng bài thảo luận hai quan điểm trái ngược mà một bên đại diện cho 'sự tiến bộ/hiện đại' và một bên đại diện cho 'giá trị cốt lõi/bảo tồn', đừng bao giờ chọn một bên và phủ định hoàn toàn bên còn lại. Hãy dùng tư duy biện chứng: Thừa nhận cái hiện đại giải quyết được phần ngọn (sản lượng, tốc độ), nhưng cái cốt lõi/truyền thống mới là cái gốc bền vững (bảo hiểm sinh học, sự sinh tồn lâu dài). Cách tư duy này tự động đẩy điểm Coherence và Task Achievement lên mức tối đa.

items.title: Writing Task 1 - UK Fuel Production (1981-2000)

fields.prompt:
Writing Task 1
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

The graph below shows the production levels of the main kinds of fuel in the UK between 1981 and 2000.

Summarize the formation by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

You should write at least 150 words.
fields.grammar:
Các cấu trúc ngữ pháp nâng cao khuyên dùng cho biểu đồ xu hướng (Band 8.5 - 9.0):
1. Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định để thêm thông tin so sánh: '..., a trend which was mirrored by...'
2. Phân từ độc lập / Rút gọn mệnh đề đồng chủ ngữ (Participle Clauses): 'Petroleum production peaked in 1999, surpassing 140 million tonnes...'
3. Cấu trúc đảo ngữ kết hợp thời gian: 'Not until the late 1980s did natural gas production begin its steep ascent.'
4. Phức hóa cấu trúc so sánh (Double Comparison / Complex Trends): 'The decline in coal production was as dramatic as the growth in natural gas extraction was rapid.'
5. Danh từ hóa kết hợp giới từ chỉ sự thay đổi: '...experienced a twofold increase in its production metrics over the 19-year period.'
fields.vocab:
1. Petroleum / Crude oil (n): Dầu mỏ / Dầu thô
2. Natural gas (n): Khí tự nhiên
3. Extraction / Production output (n): Sản lượng khai thác / đầu ra sản xuất
4. Overtake / Surpass (v): Vượt qua, qua mặt
5. Mirror a trend (v phrase): Lặp lại / Phản chiếu một xu hướng tương tự
6. Eclipse (v): Làm lu mờ, vượt trội hơn hẳn
7. Manifest a striking divergence (v phrase): Biểu lộ sự phân tách/trái ngược rõ rệt
8. Upward trajectory (n phrase): Quỹ đạo đi lên / Xu hướng tăng
9. Precipitous decline (n phrase): Sự sụt giảm nghiêm trọng, dốc đứng
10. Energy unit equivalent (n): Đơn vị năng lượng tương đương
fields.analysis:
Bước 1: Phân tích biểu đồ (Graph Analysis)
- Dạng biểu đồ: Line graph (Biểu đồ đường) có sự thay đổi theo thời gian.
- Đối tượng: 3 loại nhiên liệu chính tại Vương quốc Anh (Petroleum, Coal, Natural gas).
- Đơn vị: Triệu tấn dầu tương đương (million tonnes of oil equivalent).
- Thời gian: 1981 - 2000 (Quá khứ -> Dùng thì quá khứ đơn).

Bước 2: Xác định các đặc điểm nổi bật (Overview)
- Xu hướng chung: Khí tự nhiên và Dầu mỏ tăng tổng thể. Than đá giảm liên tục và sâu sắc.
- Điểm nhấn: Dầu mỏ luôn giữ vị trí thống trị về sản lượng trong suốt giai đoạn. Khí tự nhiên vượt qua than đá vào năm 1991.

Bước 3: Chia đoạn thân bài (Body Paragraphs)
- Thân bài 1: Mô tả chi tiết xu hướng của Dầu mỏ (Petroleum) từ lúc bắt đầu, biến động ở giữa và đạt đỉnh cuối kỳ.
- Thân bài 2: Tập trung vào sự hoán đổi vị trí đầy kịch tính giữa Khí tự nhiên (Natural gas) và Than đá (Coal) quanh mốc năm 1991.
fields.ideas:
Ý tưởng triển khai bài viết chi tiết:

1. Introduction:
- Paraphrase lại đề bài: Thay thế 'shows' bằng 'illustrates', 'production levels of the main kinds of fuel' bằng 'the extraction quantities of three primary fuel types'.

2. Overview:
- Nêu bật xu hướng tăng trưởng của dầu mỏ và khí tự nhiên đối nghịch với sự suy thoái của than đá.
- Khẳng định vị thế dẫn đầu tuyệt đối của dầu mỏ.

3. Body 1 (Petroleum):
- Năm 1981: Bắt đầu ở mức khoảng 90-100 triệu tấn.
- Giai đoạn 1981 - 1986: Tăng mạnh lên mốc 140 triệu tấn, duy trì ổn định trước khi giảm nhẹ xuống khoảng 100 triệu tấn vào năm 1990.
- Giai đoạn 1990 - 2000: Hồi phục mạnh mẽ, đạt đỉnh hơn 140 triệu tấn vào năm 1999 và khép lại ở mức sát mốc này.

4. Body 2 (Coal & Natural Gas):
- Năm 1981: Than đá đứng thứ hai (80 triệu tấn), khí tự nhiên đứng cuối (khoảng 40 triệu tấn).
- Sự thay đổi của Than đá: Lao dốc xuống mức thấp nhất vào giữa thập niên 80 (khoảng 40 triệu), phục hồi nhẹ rồi giảm dần đều xuống chỉ còn khoảng 30-35 triệu tấn vào năm 2000.
- Sự thay đổi của Khí tự nhiên: Đi ngang trong 10 năm đầu, sau đó bứt phá mạnh từ năm 1991, chính thức giao cắt và vượt qua than đá tại mốc 50 triệu tấn, tiếp tục tăng vọt chạm mốc 100 triệu tấn vào năm 2000.
fields.sample:
The line graph illustrates the production levels of three primary types of fuel—petroleum, coal, and natural gas—in the United Kingdom over a 19-year period from 1981 to 2000. Overall, the UK energy sector experienced a shift characterized by the continued dominance of petroleum, a dramatic surge in natural gas extraction, and a concomitant decline in coal production. 

Petroleum consistently maintained the highest production volume throughout the entire timeframe. Starting at approximately 90 million tonnes in 1981, its output climbed steeply to just over 140 million tonnes by 1985. Following a temporary contraction down to the 100 million tonne mark in 1990, petroleum production rebounded robustly during the 1990s, reaching a historical pinnacle of nearly 145 million tonnes in 1999 before finalizing the period slightly lower.

In stark contrast, coal and natural gas manifested fundamentally divergent trajectories, leading to a structural intersection in the early 1990s. In 1981, coal was the second most produced fuel at 80 million tonnes, whereas natural gas hovered at a modest 40 million tonnes. Coal production suffered a precipitous drop to under 40 million tonnes by 1984, and despite a brief recovery in the late 1980s, it drifted downward to end at just above 30 million tonnes in 2000. Conversely, natural gas output remained stagnant until 1990, after which it underwent an exponential expansion. It officially overtook coal in 1991 at approximately 50 million tonnes and continued its steep upward trajectory, culminating at 100 million tonnes by the end of the millennium.

Phân tích chuyên sâu bài mẫu Band 9.0:

1. Tiêu chí Task Achievement (Đáp ứng yêu cầu):
- Báo cáo đầy đủ, chính xác toàn bộ số liệu và các mốc biến động quan trọng của cả 3 đường đồ thị.
- Thực hiện các so sánh mang tính vĩ mô cực tốt, đặc biệt là điểm giao cắt (intersection) lịch sử giữa than đá và khí tự nhiên vào năm 1991.

2. Tiêu chí Coherence and Cohesion (Mạch lạc):
- Cấu trúc bài viết mạch lạc rõ ràng: Intro -> Overview -> Body 1 (Đường độc lập trên cùng) -> Body 2 (Hai đường hoán đổi vị trí phía dưới).
- Sử dụng từ nối tương phản xuất sắc: 'In stark contrast', 'Conversely', 'Following a temporary contraction'.
- Đảm bảo mạch bài trôi chảy mà không bị lặp lại cấu trúc thời gian nhàm chán.

3. Tiêu chí Lexical Resource (Từ vựng):
- Dùng đa dạng các động từ xu hướng nâng cao: 'rebounded robustly', 'manifested fundamentally divergent trajectories', 'finalizing the period', 'hovered at a modest...'.
- Cách diễn đạt đơn vị linh hoạt để tránh lặp từ.

4. Mẹo nâng band nhanh cho học viên:
Đối với những biểu đồ có các đường đan xen hoặc hoán đổi vị trí như Than đá và Khí tự nhiên, tuyệt đối không tả riêng biệt từng đường từ đầu đến cuối. Giám khảo chấm điểm cao ở khả năng nhóm thông tin. Việc viết về sự giao thoa và đổi ngôi của hai thực thể này trong cùng một đoạn văn chính là chìa khóa vàng giúp bài viết chạm mốc Band 9.0 tiêu chí Coherence và So sánh.

fields.outline:
**PART 1 OUTLINE (Chi tiết từng câu hỏi):**

**Q1: What is your full name?**
- Trả lời ngắn gọn: "My full name is ..."
- Có thể nói thêm: mọi người thường gọi tôi là gì (nickname).

**Q2: Where are you from?**
- Nêu thành phố/tỉnh, quốc gia.
- Có thể thêm: Tôi đã sống ở đó bao lâu, hoặc hiện tại tôi đang sống ở đâu.

**Q3: Do you work or study?**
- Trả lời rõ ràng: hiện tại tôi là sinh viên / nhân viên văn phòng.
- Nêu ngành học / lĩnh vực làm việc.
- Thêm 1-2 câu về cảm xúc (thích hay không, lý do).

**Q4: Do you want to travel in the outer space?**
- Bày tỏ quan điểm rõ ràng: Có / Không / Có nhưng dè dặt.
- Lý do: thích khám phá, trải nghiệm mới / sợ nguy hiểm, tốn kém.
- Có thể nêu cảm xúc cá nhân.

**Q5: What would you do if you had an opportunity?**
- Mô tả 1-2 hoạt động cụ thể:
  - Nhìn Trái Đất từ không gian.
  - Thí nghiệm khoa học.
  - Chụp ảnh, ghi lại trải nghiệm.
- Thêm cảm xúc: "I would be over the moon" (rất vui mừng).

**Q6: Have you ever learnt about stars and outer space?**
- Nêu nguồn kiến thức: sách, TV, internet, trường học.
- Nói về mức độ hiểu biết (cơ bản hay sâu).
- Ví dụ cụ thể: đã xem phim tài liệu về vũ trụ, đọc sách về thiên văn.

**Q7: Is it important to study stars?**
- Khẳng định tầm quan trọng.
- Lý do:
  - Hiểu về nguồn gốc vũ trụ.
  - Ứng dụng khoa học: dự báo thời tiết không gian, viễn thông.
  - Truyền cảm hứng cho thế hệ trẻ.

**Q8: What is your favourite star?**
- Nêu tên cụ thể: Sirius, Polaris (Sao Bắc Cực), Sun (Mặt Trời), hoặc một ngôi sao trong chòm sao.
- Lý do: vẻ đẹp, ý nghĩa văn hóa, gần gũi, sáng nhất trên bầu trời.

**Q9: Do you like wearing jewellery?**
- Trả lời có/không.
- Lý do: thích làm đẹp, phong cách / không thích vì bất tiện, dị ứng.
- Tần suất: thường xuyên hay thỉnh thoảng.

**Q10: What type of jewellery do you like?**
- Loại cụ thể: necklace (dây chuyền), ring (nhẫn), bracelet (vòng tay), earrings (bông tai).
- Chất liệu: gold, silver, gemstones.
- Phong cách: minimalist, classic, modern.

**Q11: Have you ever sent someone jewellery as a gift?**
- Trả lời có/không.
- Nếu có: tặng ai (mẹ, bạn gái, bạn thân), dịp gì (sinh nhật, lễ kỷ niệm).
- Cảm xúc của người nhận.

**Q12: Where do you buy jewellery?**
- Nơi mua: cửa hàng truyền thống, trung tâm thương mại, mua online.
- Lý do chọn nơi đó: chất lượng, giá cả, sự tiện lợi.

**Q13: Have you ever bought expensive jewellery for yourself?**
- Có hoặc chưa.
- Nếu có: món gì, giá bao nhiêu, lý do mua (tự thưởng, kỷ niệm).
- Cảm xúc khi mua và khi sử dụng.

**PART 2 OUTLINE (Cue Card):**
- **Mở đầu (15s):** Giới thiệu người đó (tên, mối quan hệ - bạn cùng lớp/đồng nghiệp).
- **Quen bao lâu & gặp như thế nào (20s):** Thời gian (hơn 2 năm). Hoàn cảnh gặp (dự án chung, lớp học).
- **Lý do thích học/làm cùng (30-40s):**
  - Phẩm chất chuyên môn: giỏi, tư duy tốt, sáng tạo.
  - Phẩm chất cá nhân: hài hước, kiên nhẫn, lắng nghe, tôn trọng.
  - Hiệu quả: bổ trợ kỹ năng, tạo động lực, đạt kết quả cao.
- **Kết luận (10-15s):** Tầm quan trọng, mong muốn tiếp tục hợp tác.

**PART 3 OUTLINE (Two-way Discussion):**
- **Q1 (Đặc điểm đồng nghiệp tốt):** Chuyên môn vững, giao tiếp tốt, đáng tin cậy, thích ứng cao, hỗ trợ, có trách nhiệm.
- **Q2 (Lợi ích):** Tăng năng suất, giảm căng thẳng, môi trường tích cực, học hỏi, gắn kết.
- **Q3 (Nếu đồng nghiệp không tốt):** Xung đột, căng thẳng, hiệu suất kém, toxic environment, nghỉ việc nhiều.
- **Q4 (Quản lý xây dựng quan hệ tốt):** Tạo lòng trung thành, tăng động lực, giảm nghỉ việc, hiệu quả nhóm tốt hơn.
- **Q5 (Cơ sở thể thao ở công ty):** Tích cực: cải thiện sức khỏe, giảm stress, gắn kết đồng nghiệp. Hạn chế: chi phí, chưa phù hợp mọi người.
- **Q6 (Người có kiến thức có được yêu thích?):** Được tôn trọng nhưng không tự động được yêu thích. Cần khiêm tốn, biết chia sẻ, giao tiếp tốt. Người giỏi mà kiêu ngạo thì khó được quý mến.

**PART 1 - FULL SAMPLE ANSWERS (Band 9.0):**

**Q1: What is your full name?**
"My full name is Nguyen Minh Anh, but most of my friends and colleagues simply call me Anh for short. It's a common name in Vietnam, but I've grown quite fond of it."

**Q2: Where are you from?**
"I'm originally from Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam. It's a vibrant city with a rich history and a perfect blend of ancient traditions and modern development. I've lived there for most of my life, though I'm currently studying in Ho Chi Minh City."

**Q3: Do you work or study?**
"I'm currently a final-year university student majoring in Business Administration. I find the field incredibly fascinating because it combines strategic thinking with practical management skills. Apart from studying, I also work part-time as a marketing assistant, which gives me valuable hands-on experience."

**Q4: Do you want to travel in the outer space?**
"Absolutely, it's been a childhood dream of mine. The idea of gazing at our planet from such a distant vantage point, seeing the curvature of the Earth against the pitch-black cosmos, is utterly breathtaking. However, I'm also aware of the immense risks and rigorous training required, so it's a cautious kind of fascination."

**Q5: What would you do if you had an opportunity?**
"If I were given that once-in-a-lifetime chance, I would probably spend most of my time observing Earth from the observation deck and taking countless photographs. I'd also love to conduct some simple experiments to understand how microgravity affects everyday objects. And of course, I would just float around and relish every single moment of weightlessness – that would be absolutely surreal."

**Q6: Have you ever learnt about stars and outer space?**
"Yes, I've always been captivated by astronomy since I was a child. I used to watch numerous documentaries about the universe, particularly those by Carl Sagan and Neil deGrasse Tyson. I also took an elective course on basic astronomy during my first year at university, which deepened my understanding of celestial phenomena like black holes and supernovas."

**Q7: Is it important to study stars?**
"Without a doubt. Studying stars isn't just about satisfying human curiosity; it has profound practical implications. For instance, understanding stellar evolution helps us comprehend the origins of elements and even predict solar activities that can affect our satellite communications and power grids on Earth. Moreover, it inspires young people to pursue science and pushes the boundaries of human knowledge."

**Q8: What is your favourite star?**
"I'd have to say Polaris, also known as the North Star. What fascinates me most is its historical significance – for centuries, it has served as a reliable navigational guide for sailors and explorers. It symbolizes constancy and direction, which I find deeply poetic. Besides, it's remarkably bright and easy to spot in the night sky."

**Q9: Do you like wearing jewellery?**
"Yes, I do, but I prefer to keep it minimal and understated. I think jewellery, when chosen wisely, can add a touch of elegance to any outfit without being overpowering. However, I'm quite selective and only wear pieces that hold sentimental value or complement my personal style."

**Q10: What type of jewellery do you like?**
"I'm particularly drawn to delicate necklaces with small pendants and simple silver rings. I find minimalist designs more versatile because they can be worn with both casual and formal attire. Occasionally, I also like elegant pearl earrings for special occasions – they exude a classic charm that never goes out of style."

**Q11: Have you ever sent someone jewellery as a gift?**
"Yes, I have. Last year, I gave my mother a beautiful gold bracelet for her birthday. She had been eyeing it for months, so I decided to surprise her. The look of joy and surprise on her face was absolutely priceless – it made the whole effort completely worthwhile. She wears it almost every day now."

**Q12: Where do you buy jewellery?**
"I usually buy jewellery from reputable brick-and-mortar stores in shopping malls because I prefer to see and touch the pieces before purchasing. Occasionally, I also browse online marketplaces for unique, handcrafted items, but I'm always cautious about authenticity and read reviews thoroughly before making a decision."

**Q13: Have you ever bought expensive jewellery for yourself?**
"Yes, I have. On my 25th birthday, I splurged on a minimalist gold necklace that I'd been eyeing for months. It wasn't just an accessory; it felt like a milestone marker for myself – a reward for all the hard work I'd put into my studies and career. Every time I wear it, it reminds me of my personal growth and independence, so it was worth every penny."

---

**PART 2 - SAMPLE ANSWER (Cue Card):**
"The person I truly admire working with is my university classmate, Minh. I've known him for over three years now, and we first met during a second-year marketing project where we were randomly assigned to the same group. What immediately struck me was his ability to remain calm and solution-oriented under pressure, even when our initial ideas fell flat.

The primary reason I enjoy collaborating with Minh is his remarkable blend of intellectual rigor and emotional intelligence. Academically, he is incredibly astute, often dissecting complex problems with such clarity that he makes the difficult seem accessible. However, what truly sets him apart is his interpersonal finesse. He has a natural talent for fostering an inclusive atmosphere, ensuring that every team member feels heard and valued. This creates a synergy where we can openly bounce ideas off each other without fear of judgment.

Furthermore, his work ethic is nothing short of inspiring. He is meticulous yet flexible, always willing to go the extra mile to refine our work, but he never imposes his views rigidly. He has this uncanny ability to turn mundane tasks into engaging challenges, which keeps our team's momentum going. Working with him isn't just about achieving good grades; it's a genuinely enriching experience that has taught me the value of patience, adaptability, and collective success. In essence, he is a catalyst that brings out the best in everyone around him, and I consider myself fortunate to have found such a compatible partner in my academic journey."

---

**PART 3 - FULL SAMPLE ANSWERS (Band 9.0):**

**Q1: What are the characteristics that good co-workers need?**
"In my view, an ideal co-worker should possess a blend of professional competence and interpersonal skills. Technically, they need to be proficient in their field and demonstrate strong problem-solving abilities. More importantly, they should be reliable and communicative – someone who can articulate their ideas clearly and, equally, listen actively to others. A good sense of humour and emotional resilience also go a long way in creating a harmonious workplace, especially during high-pressure periods. Lastly, adaptability is key, as workplaces are constantly evolving."

**Q2: What benefits if you are surrounded by good co-workers?**
"The benefits are truly multifaceted. First and foremost, good colleagues significantly boost productivity because collaboration becomes seamless and efficient. They also create a supportive environment where people feel motivated to contribute their best ideas. Moreover, having reliable co-workers reduces stress levels – knowing that you can count on others during challenging times fosters a sense of security. On a personal level, it makes the workplace enjoyable, which directly enhances job satisfaction and overall well-being."

**Q3: What would happen if the co-workers are not good?**
"If co-workers are difficult or incompetent, the consequences can be quite detrimental. Poor communication and lack of trust often lead to misunderstandings and conflicts, which can escalate into a toxic work environment. This, in turn, hampers productivity and creativity, as people become more focused on office politics than on actual work. In severe cases, high employee turnover rates become inevitable, as talented individuals tend to leave toxic environments. Ultimately, the company's reputation and bottom line can suffer significantly."

**Q4: Are there values if managers build good relationships with the workers who work underneath them?**
"Definitely. When managers invest in building genuine rapport with their subordinates, it fosters a culture of trust and mutual respect. This, in turn, can significantly boost employee engagement and loyalty, reducing turnover rates. Moreover, employees tend to be more open to feedback and more willing to go the extra mile when they feel valued as individuals, not just as cogs in a machine. It essentially creates a psychologically safe environment where innovation can thrive and people are not afraid to take calculated risks."

**Q5: Is it good for workers if the company applies sports facilities for them?**
"Absolutely, I believe this is a fantastic initiative. Providing sports facilities demonstrates that the company genuinely cares about employees' physical and mental well-being. Regular physical activity can reduce stress, improve concentration, and boost overall health, which translates into higher energy levels and better performance at work. Additionally, such facilities encourage social interaction among colleagues from different departments, fostering a stronger sense of community. However, it's important for companies to also consider employees' diverse preferences and offer a variety of options."

**Q6: Are knowledgeable people popular at work?**
"While knowledge is certainly respected, I don't think it guarantees popularity in isolation. Expertise makes someone a valuable resource, but popularity often hinges on approachability and the ability to share that knowledge without condescension. A knowledgeable person who is humble, patient, and willing to mentor others is likely to be very well-liked. Conversely, someone who flaunts their intellect or dismisses others' contributions can be perceived as arrogant and might alienate their peers, despite their brilliance. So, it's really about how they use their knowledge to uplift others."

- Giọng tự nhiên, thoải mái, nhẹ nhàng như đang trò chuyện.
- Lên giọng nhẹ ở cuối câu hỏi để thể hiện sự tương tác.
- Nhấn mạnh từ cảm xúc: "absolutely", "fascinating", "captivated", "worthwhile", "priceless".
- Xuống giọng ở cuối câu trả lời để tạo sự kết thúc tự nhiên.
- Ví dụ: *"...it was worth **every penny**."* (nhấn mạnh "every penny" và xuống giọng).

**Part 2 (Long Turn):**
- Giọng kể chuyện, có nhịp điệu, không quá nhanh.
- Tạm dừng ngắn (0.5-1 giây) sau mỗi ý chính để người nghe xử lý thông tin.
- Nhấn mạnh các tính từ miêu tả: "remarkable blend", "incredibly astute", "genuinely enriching".
- Lên giọng khi liệt kê (ví dụ: "...patient, adaptable, and collaborative...").
- Xuống giọng ở câu kết luận để tạo sự chắc chắn, dứt khoát.

**Part 3 (Discussion):**
- Giọng thuyết phục, phân tích, có trọng lượng.
- Nhấn mạnh các từ nối logic để làm rõ cấu trúc lập luận:
  - "In my view," (lên giọng nhẹ, tạm dừng)
  - "First and foremost," (nhấn mạnh từ đầu)
  - "Moreover," (chuyển ý, lên giọng)
  - "Conversely," (đối lập, nhấn mạnh)
  - "Ultimately," (kết luận, xuống giọng)
- Nhấn nhá các từ khóa quan trọng: "productivity", "toxic environment", "employee retention", "psychologically safe environment".

**3. NỐI ÂM (LINKING SOUNDS) CẦN LƯU Ý:**
- "work with him" → /wɜːk wɪð ɪm/ (nối "k" và "w", "ð" và "ɪ")
- "studying stars" → /ˈstʌd.i.ɪŋ stɑːz/ (nối "ŋ" và "s")
- "bounce ideas off each other" → /baʊns aɪˈdɪəz ɒf iːtʃ ˈʌð.ər/
- "bring out the best" → /brɪŋ aʊt ðə best/
- "keep the momentum going" → /kiːp ðə məˈmen.təm ˈɡəʊ.ɪŋ/
- "nip problems in the bud" → /nɪp ˈprɒb.ləmz ɪn ðə bʌd/
- "look up at the night sky" → /lʊk ʌp æt ðə naɪt skaɪ/
- "passed down through generations" → /pɑːst daʊn θruː ˌdʒen.əˈreɪ.ʃənz/
- "worth every penny" → /wɜːθ ˈev.ri ˈpen.i/
- "I would be over the moon" → /aɪ wʊd bi ˈəʊ.və ðə muːn/

**4. MẸO PHÁT ÂM CHUNG CHO BAND 9.0:**
- **Thay đổi cao độ:** Không nói đều đều. Lên cao khi hào hứng, xuống thấp khi nhấn mạnh ý quan trọng.
- **Tốc độ vừa phải:** Không quá nhanh (gây khó hiểu) và không quá chậm (mất tự nhiên). Khoảng 140-160 từ/phút.
- **Nhấn mạnh từ chính:** Trong mỗi câu, chọn 2-3 từ quan trọng để nhấn mạnh (kéo dài âm hoặc tăng âm lượng).
- **Dừng đúng chỗ:** Dừng sau các cụm ý, trước các từ nối, và trước khi đưa ra ví dụ.
- **Thực hành với gương:** Quan sát khẩu hình miệng khi phát âm các âm khó như /θ/ (think), /ð/ (this), /r/ (right), /l/ (light).

items.title: IELTS Mock Test 2024 January - Listening Practice Test 2 (Full 4 Parts)

fields.context:
Chắc chắn rồi, đây là script, đề bài và đáp án cho bài **Listening Practice Test 2** trong **IELTS Mock Test 2024 January** mà bạn đã yêu cầu.

---

### **THÔNG TIN CHUNG**
* **Tên bài thi:** IELTS Mock Test 2024 January - Listening Practice Test 2
* **Nguồn:** ieltsonlinetests.com
* **Số câu hỏi:** 40
* **Thời gian:** 32 phút (khoảng)

---

### ĐÁP ÁN 40 CÂU HỎI (ALL PARTS):
**Part 1 Answers:**
1. 0902429653
2. 2.50
3. Post office
4. City Museum (or the City Museum)
5. castle (or a castle)
6. Food Hall (or the Food Hall)
7. library (or a library)
8. art gallery (or the art gallery)
9. tourist office (or the tourist office)
10. Palace Hotel (or the Palace Hotel)

**Part 2 Answers:**
11. C (only local residents were invited)
12. A (by the main entrance)
13. C (he did not think it was necessary)
14. B (lack of signage)
15. A (has been reduced)
16. B (it was in the wrong place)
17. F (will be a restaurant)
18. D (a new medical center)
19. G (retained as a playground)
20. A (converted into flats)

**Part 3 Answers:**
21. Topic
22. Current
23. Thesis
24. Outline
25. Progress
26. Aspects
27. Real-life
28. Necessity
29. Style guide
30. 10%

**Part 4 Answers:**
31. A (has a long history)
32. B (was not generally accepted)
33. C (was once used for navigation)
34. Revolution
35. Sick
36. Attention
37. Bruno
38. Motion
39. Bible
40. 20 percent (or 20%)

---

## PART 1 QUESTIONS
Questions 1-5
Complete the sentences.
Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
Example: Peter consumes far too much soft drink
1. Peter and Mary’s diet will be both sensible and [practical] (Answer: Practical)
2. Every two months, they can eat [pizza(s)] (Answer: Pizza(s))
3. On Saturdays, they will go [(light) walking] (Answer: (light) walking)
4. This coming Saturday, they will go to [Pine Park] (Answer: Pine Park)
5. In every meal, there will be [fruit juice] (Answer: Fruit juice)

Questions 6-10
Choose the correct letter, C, I, or B.
C: Chocolate
I: Ice cream
B: Biscuits
Tuesdays:
- Peter's opinion: B (Biscuits)
- Mary's opinion: Question 6 (Answer: B -> Biscuits)
Thursdays:
- Peter's opinion: Question 7 (Answer: I -> Ice cream)
- Mary's opinion: Question 8 (Answer: C -> Chocolate)
Sundays:
- Peter's opinion: Question 9 (Answer: B -> Biscuits)
- Mary's opinion: Question 10 (Answer: I -> Ice cream)

## PART 1 TRANSCRIPT
PART 1
You will hear two students, Peter and Mary, discussing their new eating plan.
Peter: Okay Mary, I know I’m putting on weight with all my bad eating habits.
Mary: That’s right. Chocolate bars, pizzas, and all washed down with litres of soft drink. And with all the sugar in soft drink, I think we can say you’re definitely overindulging, don’t you think?
Peter: I know, I know. I intend to definitely stop drinking that from now on.
Mary: And that’s part of the sensible eating plan that we have agreed we need to formulate—one that we can both follow.
Peter: That’s right, sensible, and practical— allowing us to indulge in some sweet foods on occasions.
Mary: On rare occasions, and we’re going to cut out all the pizzas and hamburgers.
Peter: Well, not totally. I thought you said pizzas could be eaten once a week. You know how I like pizzas.
Mary: No. I said once every two months. Once a week was ice cream, not pizza.
Peter: Yeah, that’s because you like ice cream. I prefer pizza.
Mary: Peter, if you want to lose weight, you need to be disciplined, in both what you eat, and what you do, which brings us to the issue of exercise.
Peter: That’s right. So, jogging twice a week, and hiking on Saturdays, right?
Mary: No, hiking is Sundays, allowing Saturdays for the light walking exercise. I’ve investigated, and discovered there are a lot of walking trails around this suburb, with many beautiful places if you just look around.
Peter: So what’s happening this Saturday? A walk around the city?
Mary: That’s later in the month. This Saturday we’ll visit Pine Park.
Peter: Hill Park is nicer, with great views, too,
Mary: Yes, but we have to travel too far to reach Hill Park, so I ruled that out, and I love the smell of pines.
Peter: And what about the weekday meals? Salads every night, I suppose?
Mary: No, it’s important to vary the meals so that the food remains interesting and fun. The only common factor is the fruit juice, but otherwise we’ll have a variety of healthy fare, from salads, to fish, to lean meat.
Peter: I'd rather have meat every night, but you’re the boss.
Mary: If you want to lose weight, you’ll have to accept this program, okay?
Peter: Okay.
Peter: Now Mary, you said we could have a little treat in our diet plan three times a week: specifically, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays.
Mary: Yes. A very small treat, but something to reward us for all the discipline shown. Such rewards will motivate us to continue the diet.
Peter: So, on Tuesdays, what can I choose?
Mary: You have a choice between a small serving of chocolate, ice cream, or biscuits.
Peter: Okay, well, I’ll go for the biscuits. I love those crunchy little things with my cup of tea. So do you, right?
Mary: I do indeed, so I’ll have them, too, saving the ice cream for later.
Peter: But I know how much you like ice cream, so why don’t you save it for the end of the week? That will give you the motivation to keep going, and you can have chocolate midweek?
Mary: That’s a good idea, but I think the most important thing is for you and I to eat different things on those other two days.
Peter: Well, if you think that way, I’ll eat the ice cream on Thursdays, not the chocolate. Okay?
Mary: Well, if you’re having that, then I can’t have ice cream. In order to be different, I’ll have the chocolate.
Peter: So, we can compare our different snacks, and maybe even share a little with each other.
Mary: Exactly! And the variety and fun involved will take our minds of wanting more.
Peter: Eating for fun! A good idea!
Mary: And then you can have the chocolate on Sunday, right?
Peter: But I like biscuits? Actually, I want biscuits again—to have with my cup of tea.
Mary: But you have the biscuits on Monday, remember, and we can’t repeat.
Peter: Ah come on! This isn’t fixed in concrete. I can have them again instead of chocolate. You might like variety, but I don’t. I’m a creature of habit.
Mary: Well, the whole point of this was to taste different snacks, but if you want the same thing, okay. I, for one, am sticking to the original plan, with ice cream to finish the week, and not another dose of chocolate.



---
*Lưu ý: Các phần Part 2, Part 3, Part 4 chưa lấy đủ đề bài và transcript hoàn chỉnh do đã dừng tiến trình crawl theo yêu cầu.*
fields.spelling:
**LỖI CHÍNH TẢ VÀ BẪY PHÁT ÂM CẦN LƯU Ý:**

1. **Tên riêng và địa danh (cần viết hoa chính xác):**
   - Peter, Mary (Part 1)
   - Pine Park (không phải 'Pinepark' hay 'Pine Park' - viết rời, viết hoa cả hai chữ)
   - Stanfield (Part 2 - viết liền, một chữ 'S')
   - Andrea, Bella, Cathy (Part 2 - phân biệt âm /ˈkæθi/ và /ˈbɛlə/)
   - Eric, Ms Harris (Part 3)
   - Nicolaus Copernicus (Part 4 - lưu ý 'Coper-nicus' chứ không phải 'Copernicus' với 'e')
   - Aristarchus, Galileo, Giordano Bruno (Part 4)

2. **Từ dễ nhầm lẫn do phát âm tương tự (homophones):**
   - **practical** (thiết thực) vs **practicable** (khả thi) - trong script: "sensible and practical"
   - **padded** (có đệm) vs **pathed** (có lối đi) - script: "padded walls"
   - **disinfect** (khử trùng) vs **disinfectant** (chất khử trùng) - script: "we disinfect every surface"
   - **germs** (vi trùng) vs **terms** (điều khoản) - script: "ensure germs are not transmitted"
   - **thesis** (luận điểm) vs **theses** (số nhiều) - script: "think of a thesis"
   - **outline** (dàn bài) vs **outlook** (quan điểm) - script: "you'll need an outline"
   - **progress** (sự tiến triển) vs **process** (quá trình) - script: "there must be a sense of progress"
   - **aspects** (khía cạnh) vs **expects** (mong đợi) - script: "many aspects to consider"
   - **necessity** (sự cần thiết) vs **necessary** (cần thiết) - script: "That's an academic necessity"
   - **Bruno** /ˈbruːnəʊ/ vs **Bella** /ˈbɛlə/ - phân biệt rõ âm đầu và âm cuối

3. **Số đếm và phần trăm dễ nhầm:**
   - **10%** (Part 3) - không nhầm với '15%' hay '20%' (đều xuất hiện trong bài)
   - **20 percent** (Part 4) - viết bằng chữ, không viết '20%' nếu yêu cầu ONE WORD OR A NUMBER
   - **every two months** (Part 1) - không nhầm với 'once a week' hay 'twice a week'

4. **Từ có hai âm tiết dễ nhầm trọng âm:**
   - **'practical** /ˈpræk.tɪ.kəl/ - nhấn âm 1
   - **dis'infect** /ˌdɪs.ɪnˈfekt/ - nhấn âm 3
   - **ne'cessity** /nəˈses.ə.ti/ - nhấn âm 2
   - **'outline** /ˈaʊt.laɪn/ - nhấn âm 1
   - **'progress** (danh từ) /ˈprəʊ.ɡres/ - nhấn âm 1
   - **revo'lution** /ˌrev.əˈluː.ʃən/ - nhấn âm 3

5. **Lỗi chính tả thường gặp:**
   - 'disinfect' (khử trùng) - chỉ có một 'f'
   - 'padded' (có đệm) - viết hai chữ 'd'
   - 'necessity' - có hai chữ 's' và một 'c'
   - 'Bruno' - không phải 'Bruneau'
   - 'style guide' - viết rời, không viết liền 'styleguide'
   - 'real-life' - có dấu gạch ngang
   - 'Pine Park' - viết hoa, viết rời

fields.transcript:
**PHÂN TÍCH BẪY TRONG TRANSCRIPT & CHIẾN LƯỢC NGHE:**

**PART 1 - Bẫy thông tin (Distractors):**

- **Question 1:** Peter đề cập "sensible and practical" - nhưng cả hai đều là tính từ, chỉ có 'practical' là đáp án (từ khóa nối 'and' - cả hai đều quan trọng, nhưng câu hỏi yêu cầu từ còn thiếu).
- **Question 2:** Peter nói "once a week" nhưng Mary đính chính lại "once every two months" - đây là bẫy đảo ngược thông tin. Cần nghe toàn bộ đoạn hội thoại, không chỉ câu đầu.
- **Question 3:** Hiking được đề cập cho Chủ Nhật, nhưng câu hỏi hỏi Thứ Bảy: "Saturdays for the light walking exercise" - từ khóa 'light walking' nằm ở giữa đoạn, dễ bỏ lỡ.
- **Question 4:** Peter gợi ý "Hill Park" nhưng Mary đã "ruled that out" và quyết định "Pine Park" - bẫy câu phủ định 'ruled out' và thay thế bằng địa điểm khác.
- **Question 5:** Nhiều loại thức ăn được đề cập (salads, fish, lean meat) nhưng "the only common factor is the fruit juice" - từ khóa 'common factor' giúp xác định câu trả lời duy nhất.
- **Questions 6-10:** Bẫy lịch trình và sở thích khác nhau. Peter và Mary có lựa chọn khác nhau cho cùng một ngày:
  - Tuesday: Peter chọn B (biscuits), Mary cũng chọn B (đồng ý với Peter) → Q6 đáp án B
  - Thursday: Peter chọn I (ice cream), Mary chọn C (chocolate) để khác biệt → Q7 = I, Q8 = C
  - Sunday: Peter muốn B (biscuits) lần nữa, Mary vẫn chọn I (ice cream) → Q9 = B, Q10 = I
  - Lưu ý: Cần theo dõi cả hai quan điểm, không chỉ một người.

**PART 2 - Bẫy thông tin (Distractors):**

- **Question 11-12:** "every room has padded walls" và "padding extends around all corners" - hai thông tin liền kề nhưng hỏi riêng lẻ. Q11 = padded, Q12 = corners.
- **Question 13-14:** "all of them have a special skill" và "have a wealth of learning toys" - cần phân biệt 'skill' (kỹ năng) và 'toys' (đồ chơi).
- **Question 15-16:** "we disinfect every surface" và "germs are not transmitted" - động từ 'disinfect' ở đầu câu, danh từ 'germs' ở cuối câu, dễ trộn lẫn.
- **Questions 17-20 (Matching):**
  - Cathy "has her own family — two little girls" → Q17 = C
  - Andrea "will sometimes spend the night here" → Q18 = A
  - Cathy "deal with the particularly quiet and introverted children" → Q19 = C
  - Bella "can make some of the best cakes in town" → Q20 = B
  - Bẫy: Thông tin về Bella ngủ tại trung tâm (dùng để gây nhiễu, nhưng Andrea mới là người ngủ qua đêm). "often sleeps" (Andrea) vs "spend long hours" (Bella, Cathy).

**PART 3 - Bẫy thông tin (Distractors):**

- **Question 21:** "Start with a topic, but not one that I necessarily suggest, but one that you want to explore" → 'topic' là đáp án, không phải 'area' hay 'thesis'.
- **Question 22:** "Break it into various current areas of discussion" → 'current' là tính từ bổ nghĩa cho 'areas'.
- **Question 23:** "You'll have to think of a thesis" → 'thesis' được nhấn mạnh, là từ chính xác.
- **Question 24:** "you'll need an outline" → 'outline' (không phải 'flowchart' hay 'spider graph' - chỉ là ví dụ về hình thức).
- **Question 25:** "there must be a sense of progress" → 'progress' là danh từ chỉ sự tiến triển.
- **Questions 26-30 (Summary):**
  - Q26: "many aspects to consider" → 'aspects'
  - Q27: "examples, from real-life" → 'real-life' (có gạch nối)
  - Q28: "give a reference. That's an academic necessity" → 'necessity'
  - Q29: "as written in the university style guide" → 'style guide' (viết rời, số ít)
  - Q30: "perhaps 10% either way should be acceptable" → '10%' (viết số, có dấu %) - lưu ý: câu hỏi yêu cầu NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER, nên '10%' được chấp nhận.

**PART 4 - Bẫy thông tin (Distractors):**

- **Q31:** Đoạn đầu nói "all pre-modern civilisations drew this conclusion" → chứng tỏ geocentrism "has a long history" (A). Đáp án B sai vì geocentrism và heliocentrism khác nhau. Đáp án C sai vì Aristarchus đề xuất heliocentrism từ thế kỷ 3 BC, không phải 'took time to be deduced' cho geocentrism.
- **Q32:** "Aristarchus ... proposed heliocentrism, but received little support" và "Copernicus ... waited until the last year ... to release his findings" → heliocentrism "was not generally accepted" (B). A sai vì được đề xuất từ thế kỷ 3 BC (không phải 'recently'). C sai vì geocentrism mới 'fitted the views of the church'.
- **Q33:** "serve the primary purpose of navigation for sailing ships" → bầu trời đêm "was once used for navigation" (C). A sai vì "simple revolution ... proved not so simple at all". B sai vì có nhiều hiện tượng phức tạp (planets, comets).
- **Q34:** "Copernican revolution" → 'revolution' viết thường, số ít.
- **Q35:** "waited until the last year of his life, when he was sick and dying" → 'sick' (không phải 'old' hay 'dying' vì chỉ cho phép ONE WORD).
- **Q36:** "received scant attention" → 'attention' (sự chú ý).
- **Q37:** "the surname Bruno, Giordano Bruno. who was burnt at the stake" → 'Bruno' (tên họ).
- **Q38:** "the sun ... was itself in motion around a common centre of gravity" → 'motion' (chuyển động).
- **Q39:** "literal interpretations of the Bible, which is the cornerstone" → 'Bible' (Kinh thánh).
- **Q40:** "surveys have revealed that up to 10% of British people, 12% of Europeans. 20% of the USA" → hỏi về nước Mỹ, đáp án '20 percent' (có thể viết '20%' nhưng yêu cầu ONE WORD OR A NUMBER nên '20' được chấp nhận, nhưng script có cả hai nên nên viết '20%' hoặc '20' tùy theo hướng dẫn).
fields.explanation:
**GIẢI THÍCH CHI TIẾT ĐÁP ÁN CHO TỪNG CÂU HỎI:**

**PART 1:**

1. **Đáp án: practical**
   - Câu thoại: *"That's right, sensible, and practical — allowing us to indulge in some sweet foods on occasions."*
   - Giải thích: Peter và Mary thống nhất chế độ ăn vừa hợp lý (sensible) vừa thiết thực (practical). Câu hỏi yêu cầu từ còn thiếu sau 'sensible and', đáp án là 'practical'.

2. **Đáp án: pizza(s)**
   - Câu thoại: *"No. I said once every two months. Once a week was ice cream, not pizza."*
   - Giải thích: Mary sửa lại Peter rằng pizza chỉ được ăn mỗi hai tháng một lần. Đáp án chấp nhận 'pizza' hoặc 'pizzas' vì không ảnh hưởng nghĩa.

3. **Đáp án: (light) walking**
   - Câu thoại: *"No, hiking is Sundays, allowing Saturdays for the light walking exercise."*
   - Giải thích: Thứ Bảy dành cho đi bộ nhẹ nhàng. Đáp án 'light walking' hoặc 'walking' đều được chấp nhận (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS).

4. **Đáp án: Pine Park**
   - Câu thoại: *"This Saturday we'll visit Pine Park."* và *"Hill Park is nicer ... but we have to travel too far ... so I ruled that out"*
   - Giải thích: Mary chọn Pine Park vì Hill Park quá xa. Đáp án cần viết hoa đúng tên riêng.

5. **Đáp án: fruit juice**
   - Câu thoại: *"The only common factor is the fruit juice, but otherwise we'll have a variety of healthy fare."*
   - Giải thích: Điểm chung duy nhất trong mỗi bữa ăn là nước trái cây. Các món khác thay đổi (salads, fish, lean meat).

6. **Đáp án: B**
   - Câu thoại: *"Peter: Okay, well, I'll go for the biscuits. ... Mary: I do indeed, so I'll have them, too"*
   - Giải thích: Cả Peter và Mary đều chọn bánh quy (Biscuits - B) vào Thứ Ba.

7. **Đáp án: I**
   - Câu thoại: *"Peter: Well, if you think that way, I'll eat the ice cream on Thursdays, not the chocolate."*
   - Giải thích: Peter chọn kem (Ice cream - I) vào Thứ Năm.

8. **Đáp án: C**
   - Câu thoại: *"Mary: Well, if you're having that, then I can't have ice cream. I order to be different, I'll have the chocolate."*
   - Giải thích: Mary chọn sô-cô-la (Chocolate - C) để khác biệt với Peter.

9. **Đáp án: B**
   - Câu thoại: *"Peter: Actually, I want biscuits again—to have with my cup of tea. ... I can have them again instead of chocolate."*
   - Giải thích: Peter muốn ăn bánh quy (B) vào Chủ Nhật, không phải sô-cô-la.

10. **Đáp án: I**
    - Câu thoại: *"Mary: I, for one, am sticking to the original plan, with ice cream to finish the week"*
    - Giải thích: Mary vẫn chọn kem (I) vào Chủ Nhật theo kế hoạch ban đầu.

**PART 2:**

11. **Đáp án: padded**
    - Câu thoại: *"Look around and you'll see that every room has padded walls."*
    - Giải thích: Tường được bọc đệm để đảm bảo an toàn cho trẻ.

12. **Đáp án: corners**
    - Câu thoại: *"This padding extends around all corners — that is, the areas most likely to bruise and cut your active little child."*
    - Giải thích: Đệm được bọc quanh các góc, nơi dễ gây thương tích nhất.

13. **Đáp án: special skill**
    - Câu thoại: *"all of them have a special skill, which they can impart to your child"*
    - Giải thích: Mỗi nhân viên có một kỹ năng đặc biệt để truyền đạt cho trẻ.

14. **Đáp án: learning toys**
    - Câu thoại: *"have a wealth of learning toys, specially designed to develop your child's potential."*
    - Giải thích: Trung tâm có nhiều đồ chơi giáo dục.

15. **Đáp án: disinfect**
    - Câu thoại: *"we disinfect every surface at the end of every day, using a special disinfectant wash."*
    - Giải thích: Họ khử trùng mọi bề mặt hàng ngày.

16. **Đáp án: germs**
    - Câu thoại: *"we ask him or her to wear a face mask to ensure germs are not transmitted."*
    - Giải thích: Quy trình nhằm hạn chế lây lan vi trùng.

17. **Đáp án: C**
    - Câu thoại: *"Cathy has her own family — two little girls"*
    - Giải thích: Cathy có con riêng (two little girls).

18. **Đáp án: A**
    - Câu thoại: *"Andrea, who will sometimes spend the night here, staying in our overnight room."*
    - Giải thích: Andrea thường ngủ lại trung tâm qua đêm.

19. **Đáp án: C**
    - Câu thoại: *"We let Cathy, though, deal with the particularly quiet and introverted children"*
    - Giải thích: Cathy được giao phụ trách trẻ nhút nhát, hướng nội.

20. **Đáp án: B**
    - Câu thoại: *"Cathy often gets these from Bella, who can make some of the best cakes in town."*
    - Giải thích: Bella nấu ăn ngon, đặc biệt là bánh ngọt.

**PART 3:**

21. **Đáp án: topic**
    - Câu thoại: *"Start with a topic, but not one that I necessarily suggest, but one that you want to explore."*
    - Giải thích: Bắt đầu bằng chủ đề bạn yêu thích.

22. **Đáp án: current**
    - Câu thoại: *"Break it into various current areas of discussion and relevance."*
    - Giải thích: Tập trung vào lĩnh vực hiện thời, có liên quan.

23. **Đáp án: thesis**
    - Câu thoại: *"You'll have to think of a thesis, and this statement could be of several types."*
    - Giải thích: Viết câu luận điểm (thesis statement).

24. **Đáp án: outline**
    - Câu thoại: *"This means you'll need an outline. This could be written as a flowchart, or spider graph"*
    - Giải thích: Tạo dàn bài (outline) trước khi viết.

25. **Đáp án: progress**
    - Câu thoại: *"there must be a sense of progress, in, more or less, a straight line, towards a goal."*
    - Giải thích: Đảm bảo sự tiến triển rõ ràng hướng tới mục tiêu.

26. **Đáp án: aspects**
    - Câu thoại: *"Oh, there are many aspects to consider"*
    - Giải thích: Có nhiều khía cạnh liên quan đến việc viết bài luận tốt.

27. **Đáp án: real-life**
    - Câu thoại: *"For that, you need examples, from real-life, to illustrate your points or sub-points."*
    - Giải thích: Cần ví dụ từ thực tế để minh họa.

28. **Đáp án: necessity**
    - Câu thoại: *"you must give a reference. That's an academic necessity"*
    - Giải thích: Trích dẫn nguồn là một yêu cầu bắt buộc trong học thuật.

29. **Đáp án: style guide**
    - Câu thoại: *"as written in the university style guide, such as leaving appropriate margins, using double spacing, Arial font, and so on."*
    - Giải thích: Định dạng theo hướng dẫn của trường đại học.

30. **Đáp án: 10%**
    - Câu thoại: *"perhaps 10% either way should be acceptable."*
    - Giải thích: Số lượng từ có thể dao động khoảng 10%.

**PART 4:**

31. **Đáp án: A**
    - Câu thoại: *"all pre-modern civilisations drew this conclusion. We now know ... but historically, it took quite a while for this to be deduced."*
    - Giải thích: Thuyết địa tâm có lịch sử lâu dài, được tin tưởng từ thời tiền hiện đại. Đáp án A đúng.

32. **Đáp án: B**
    - Câu thoại: *"Aristarchus ... proposed heliocentrism, but received little support. Similarly, throughout subsequent history, isolated individuals proposed this new idea, but again, no one was listening."* và *"Copernicus ... feared the consequences"*
    - Giải thích: Thuyết nhật tâm không được chấp nhận rộng rãi (B). A sai vì không phải 'recently' (đã có từ thế kỷ 3 BC). C sai vì thuyết địa tâm mới phù hợp với giáo hội.

33. **Đáp án: C**
    - Câu thoại: *"In order to predict the motion of the planets, and accurately serve the primary purpose of navigation for sailing ships, increasingly elaborate mathematical models were needed."*
    - Giải thích: Bầu trời đêm từng được dùng để định vị hàng hải. A sai vì 'not so simple at all'. B sai vì có nhiều hiện tượng phức tạp.

34. **Đáp án: revolution**
    - Câu thoại: *"This event is sometimes referred to as the Copernican revolution."*
    - Giải thích: Thuật ngữ chỉ cuộc cách mạng Copernicus.

35. **Đáp án: sick**
    - Câu thoại: *"he waited until the last year of his life, when he was sick and dying, to release his findings."*
    - Giải thích: Ông ốm yếu trong năm cuối đời. Từ 'sick' được chọn vì chỉ được ONE WORD.

36. **Đáp án: attention**
    - Câu thoại: *"the book received scant attention in the subsequent decades"*
    - Giải thích: Cuốn sách không được nhiều sự chú ý.

37. **Đáp án: Bruno**
    - Câu thoại: *"as did a fellow Italian, with the surname Bruno, Giordano Bruno, who was burnt at the stake"*
    - Giải thích: Bruno bị thiêu sống vì ủng hộ thuyết nhật tâm.

38. **Đáp án: motion**
    - Câu thoại: *"a work which implied that even the sun, around which the Earth circled, was itself in motion around a common centre of gravity."*
    - Giải thích: Ngay cả Mặt Trời cũng đang chuyển động.

39. **Đáp án: Bible**
    - Câu thoại: *"Modern geocentrism is usually the result of literal interpretations of the Bible, which is the cornerstone of these people's beliefs."*
    - Giải thích: Thuyết địa tâm hiện đại dựa trên Kinh Thánh.

40. **Đáp án: 20 percent** (hoặc '20' tùy theo yêu cầu ONE WORD OR A NUMBER)
    - Câu thoại: *"20% of the USA"*
    - Giải thích: 20% người Mỹ tin vào thuyết địa tâm. Đáp án có thể viết là '20' hoặc '20%' nhưng script yêu cầu ONE WORD OR A NUMBER nên '20' là an toàn nhất.
