fields.sentence:
1. Phân tích câu phức (Passage 1 - Đoạn 4): 'He often missed classes and used the time to study physics on his own or to play the violin instead.'
- Cấu trúc: Chủ ngữ 'He', động từ chính 'missed', theo sau là một động từ thứ hai 'used' cùng cấu trúc bổ ngữ chỉ mục đích 'to study physics... or to play the violin instead'.
- Dịch nghĩa: Anh ấy thường xuyên trốn học và dùng thời gian đó để tự nghiên cứu vật lý hoặc chơi đàn violin.

2. Phân tích câu phức (Passage 3 - Đoạn 9): 'We all know that in many countries languages are constantly borrowing words and expressions from English into their own language, so why not borrow fillers too?'
- Cấu trúc: Câu chứa mệnh đề danh từ làm tân ngữ cho 'know' ('that in many countries...'). Mệnh đề chính kết thúc bằng câu hỏi tu từ với cấu trúc 'why not + verb' thể hiện sự suy luận hợp lý.
- Dịch nghĩa: Tất cả chúng ta đều biết rằng ở nhiều quốc gia, các ngôn ngữ liên tục vay mượn từ ngữ và cách diễn đạt từ tiếng Anh vào ngôn ngữ của chính họ, vậy tại sao không vay mượn cả các từ đệm nữa?
fields.tips:
1. Dạng bài YES/NO/NOT GIVEN: Lưu ý rằng NOT GIVEN là khi thông tin không có trong bài, còn FALSE là thông tin trái ngược. Đừng 'nhìn hình đoán chữ', phải tìm đúng từ khóa trong văn bản.
2. Dạng bài Multiple Choice: Loại trừ các đáp án có từ ngữ cực đoan như 'only', 'all', 'never' nếu bài đọc không dùng các từ đó. Hãy ưu tiên các đáp án có tính chất diễn đạt khái quát và chính xác.
3. Dạng bài điền từ (Summary/Gap Fill): Kiểm tra loại từ (danh từ, động từ, tính từ) để điền vào chỗ trống cho đúng ngữ pháp. Chú ý các từ đứng trước và sau chỗ trống để suy luận.
4. Matching Information: Đây là dạng bài không theo trình tự đoạn văn. Hãy quét qua toàn bộ các đoạn một lượt để tìm tên riêng, số liệu hoặc thuật ngữ khoa học trước khi đọc kỹ chi tiết.
fields.explanation:
Lời giải chi tiết và dẫn chứng nguồn chứa câu trả lời:

[PART 1: ALBERT EINSTEIN]
- Câu 1: TRUE. Đoạn 1: '...his theories... are of great importance to many branches of physics and astronomy.'
- Câu 2: TRUE. Đoạn 3: '...his family were worried that he would never start to speak.'
- Câu 3: FALSE. Đoạn 3: '...no other force (such as the wind) could have been moving it.'
- Câu 4: FALSE. Đoạn 4: 'But Einstein did not like the teaching there either [Munich/Zurich].'
- Câu 5: NOT GIVEN. Bài đọc nói Einstein chơi violin nhưng không nhắc việc ông tự học hay học từ người khác.
- Câu 6: FALSE. Đoạn 5: Con gái ông mất năm 2 tuổi, con trai (Eduard) mắc tâm thần phân liệt, bài không ghi con gái mắc bệnh này.
- Câu 7: FALSE. Đoạn 5: Chỉ đến khi cháu gái tìm thấy thư trong hộp giày, mọi người mới biết sự tồn tại của con gái ông.
- Câu 8: NOT GIVEN. Bài nói ông chuyển đến Mỹ năm 1933 và mất ở đó, không nhắc đến quốc tịch.
- Câu 9: pointed north. Đoạn 3: '...why the needle always pointed north...'
- Câu 10: on his own. Đoạn 4: '...used the time to study physics on his own...'
- Câu 11: B. Đoạn 5: '...whose name we do not know...'
- Câu 12: A. Đoạn 4: 'His teachers did not have a good opinion of him...'
- Câu 13: B. Đoạn 2: 'His family was Jewish...'

[PART 2: DRINKING FILTERED WATER]
- Câu 14: A. Đoạn A tóm tắt vấn đề chất lượng nước và sự cần thiết của nước lọc.
- Câu 15: F. Đoạn F liệt kê các loại lọc (activated carbon, ozone).
- Câu 16: E. Đoạn E giải thích nước sạch giúp cơ thể loại bỏ độc tố ('rid itself of toxins').
- Câu 17: G. Đoạn G khuyên dùng 'Consumer Confidence Report' để quyết định loại máy lọc.
- Câu 18: C. Đoạn C nêu thủy ngân (mercury) liên quan đến nhiều dị ứng ('allergies and cancers').
- Câu 19: D. Đoạn D nêu chì (lead) thường có trong đường ống cũ ('pipes in old houses').
- Câu 20: B. Đoạn B nói các hóa chất như clo, brom khử trùng ('disinfect').
- Câu 21: TRUE. Đoạn A: '...quality of water that we drink every day has an important effect on our health.'
- Câu 22: FALSE. Đoạn B: 'Filtered water is typically free of such water disinfectant chemicals.'
- Câu 23: TRUE. Đoạn B: '...may bring about poisoning of the brain, heart, kidneys and liver.'
- Câu 24: FALSE. Đoạn A: 'Filtered water is healthier than tap water [which is full of contaminants].'
- Câu 25: NOT GIVEN. Không có dữ liệu về răng giả.
- Câu 26: NOT GIVEN. Không có dữ liệu về trầm cảm và mất nước.

[PART 3: SPEECH DYSFLUENCY AND POPULAR FILLERS]
- Câu 27: TRUE. Đoạn 2: 'Fillers are parts of speech that are not generally recognized as meaningful...'
- Câu 28: TRUE. Đoạn 3: 'Research... has shown that fillers change across cultures...'
- Câu 29: FALSE. Đoạn 2: '...they occur quite regularly in everyday conversation...'
- Câu 30: FALSE. Đoạn 5: '...men use 'uh' more than women, no matter their age.'
- Câu 31: NOT GIVEN. Chỉ nói về Mỹ, Anh, Scotland, Đức... không nói về Tây Ban Nha.
- Câu 32: TRUE. Đoạn 5: 'scientists used to think that fillers had more to do with the amount of time a speaker pauses...'
- Câu 33: NOT GIVEN. Không nói về bối cảnh thảo luận của Liberman.
- Câu 34: FALSE. Đoạn 8: '...young people and women prefer it [um]... it is just one of those things.'
- Câu 35: D. Đoạn 2: 'Fillers are normally avoided on television and in films...'
- Câu 36: B. Đoạn 4: '...Liberman... 'um' generally comes before a longer or more important pause than 'uh'.'
- Câu 37: B. Đoạn 5: '...fillers had more to do... with who the speaker is.'
- Câu 38: A. Đoạn 7: '...how such a trend might have gone from one language to another... it is a likely story.'
- Câu 39: D. Đoạn 7: 'Women and young people are typically the pioneers of most language changes.'
- Câu 40: D. Đoạn 8: 'It’s just one of those things.' (Sự ngẫu nhiên/tình cờ).

fields.grammar:
Task 1:
- Cấu trúc so sánh: 'While Poland recorded the highest unemployment rates for both age groups, Denmark displayed the lowest figures across the board.'
- Mệnh đề quan hệ: 'The youth unemployment rate, which reflects the jobless percentage for those aged 15-24, was consistently higher than the overall unemployment rate in all five countries.'
- Cấu trúc chỉ sự tương phản: 'In contrast to the overall unemployment figures, which remained relatively low in Hungary and Italy, the youth sector faced significantly more challenging conditions.'
Task 2:
- Cấu trúc giả định: 'Were city planners to prioritize green spaces and pollution control, many of the health detriments associated with urban living could be effectively mitigated.'
- Đảo ngữ nhấn mạnh: 'Not only does city life offer unparalleled access to specialized healthcare, but it also provides a fast-paced environment that can stimulate active lifestyles.'
- Cấu trúc nhượng bộ: 'Although urban areas are often criticized for their sedentary nature and environmental pollutants, they simultaneously provide infrastructures that facilitate a healthy lifestyle for those who choose to utilize them.'
fields.vocab:
Task 1 (Tả số liệu):
- Youth unemployment rate (n phrase): Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp ở thanh thiếu niên
- Overall percentage (n phrase): Tỷ lệ chung / tổng thể
- Consistently higher (adj): Cao hơn một cách đồng nhất
- Pronounced disparity (n phrase): Sự chênh lệch rõ rệt

Task 2 (Viết luận):
- Urban sprawl (n): Sự mở rộng đô thị
- Sedentary lifestyle (n phrase): Lối sống thụ động / ít vận động
- Environmental pollutants (n phrase): Các chất gây ô nhiễm môi trường
- Access to healthcare facilities (n phrase): Khả năng tiếp cận các cơ sở y tế

fields.analysis:
Task 1:
- Dạng biểu đồ: Biểu đồ cột nhóm (Grouped Bar Chart) so sánh 2 nhóm dữ liệu.
- Đối tượng: Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp ở 5 quốc gia (Ba Lan, Ý, Hungary, Đức, Đan Mạch) năm 2005 giữa nhóm thanh niên (15-24 tuổi) và tỷ lệ chung.
- Phân tích: Tất cả 5 quốc gia đều có tỷ lệ thất nghiệp thanh niên cao hơn tỷ lệ chung. Ba Lan cao nhất, Đan Mạch thấp nhất. Khoảng cách chênh lệch lớn nhất nằm ở Ý và Hungary.

Task 2:
- Dạng bài: Opinion Essay (To what extent do you agree or disagree?).
- Lập trường: Đồng ý một phần (Partially Agree). Sống ở thành phố có cả rủi ro (ô nhiễm, lối sống ít vận động) và lợi thế (chăm sóc y tế tốt, tiện ích sống).
fields.ideas:
Task 1:
- Introduction: Paraphrase đề bài.
- Overview: Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp thanh niên luôn vượt xa tỷ lệ chung ở mọi quốc gia. Ba Lan đứng đầu trong khi Đan Mạch là nơi có thị trường lao động ổn định nhất.
- Body 1: Mô tả nhóm có tỷ lệ thất nghiệp cao nhất: Ba Lan (thanh niên ~34%, chung ~27%) và Ý (thanh niên ~27%, chung ~15%). Nhấn mạnh sự chênh lệch (gap) tại Ý rất lớn.
- Body 2: Mô tả nhóm còn lại: Hungary (~24% so với ~13%), Đức (~23% so với ~20%), và Đan Mạch là thấp nhất với thanh niên (~12%) và chung (~8%).

Task 2:
- Introduction: Dẫn dắt xu hướng đô thị hóa. Lập trường: Tác động của thành phố đối với sức khỏe là 'con dao hai lưỡi'.
- Body 1 (Tại sao nói thành phố xấu cho sức khỏe): Ô nhiễm không khí, tiếng ồn, không gian chật hẹp. Nhịp sống nhanh dẫn đến căng thẳng (stress), đồ ăn nhanh phổ biến, ít vận động.
- Body 2 (Tại sao thành phố có lợi cho sức khỏe): Tiếp cận y tế chuyên sâu, công nghệ hiện đại. Các công trình như phòng gym, công viên, trung tâm thể thao phát triển giúp con người rèn luyện sức khỏe tốt hơn vùng nông thôn nếu họ có ý thức.
- Conclusion: Khẳng định sống ở đâu không quan trọng bằng cách sống. Thành phố cung cấp điều kiện tốt hơn nhưng đòi hỏi con người phải kỷ luật để tránh các tác hại.
fields.sample:
Task 1:
The bar chart compares the unemployment rates among youth (aged 15-24) with the overall unemployment figures in five different European countries in 2005.

Overall, it is evident that the unemployment rate for young people was consistently higher than the overall unemployment percentage across all five nations surveyed. Poland recorded the highest figures in both categories, whereas Denmark enjoyed the most stable labor market.

Poland exhibited the most significant unemployment issues, with the youth rate reaching approximately 34%, while the overall rate stood at around 27%. Italy also showed a pronounced disparity; while the overall unemployment rate was relatively modest at 15%, the rate for those aged 15-24 was significantly higher, at approximately 27%. A similar gap was observed in Hungary, where the youth unemployment figure hit 24%, compared to roughly 13% for the general population.

Germany presented a smaller gap, with 23% of young people unemployed, while the overall unemployment rate was 20%. Finally, Denmark demonstrated the best performance among the countries listed. Its youth unemployment rate was the lowest, at approximately 12%, and its overall unemployment rate also registered the lowest figure, at just 8%.


Task 2:
It is widely perceived that residing in modern, densely populated urban centers is detrimental to an individual’s health. While there are legitimate concerns regarding the environmental and psychological pressures of city living, I believe that urban areas also offer significant advantages that can foster a healthy lifestyle. Therefore, I disagree with the view that big cities are inherently 'bad' for health.

Those who argue that cities are unhealthy often point to the negative environmental impacts of urban life. Air pollution, primarily caused by vehicle emissions and industrial activity, is a persistent concern in many metropolises, contributing to respiratory issues. Furthermore, the high-pressure, fast-paced nature of urban professional life frequently leads to excessive stress, which is a key factor in many chronic illnesses. The convenience of fast food and the sedentary nature of office work in cities can also lead to obesity and related disorders, as outdoor physical activities may be curtailed by lack of space or the urban sprawl.

However, this pessimistic perspective overlooks the substantial health advantages inherent in city living. Large cities house the best-equipped hospitals and a wide range of specialized medical practitioners, ensuring that residents have immediate access to world-class healthcare if they fall ill. Additionally, cities often boast a greater density of gyms, sports clubs, and public parks, which can provide excellent opportunities for fitness if one chooses to utilize them. For individuals who are conscious of their well-being, the city provides the necessary infrastructure to live a healthier life than is often possible in isolated rural areas, where medical facilities and fitness centers may be scarce.

Ultimately, whether city life is harmful or beneficial depends more on the lifestyle choices of the individual than on the urban environment itself. While a resident might succumb to the stresses of city living, another may leverage the city's resources to maintain an active and healthy existence. It is not the city that dictates health outcomes, but rather the degree of self-discipline an individual exercises within it.

In conclusion, while big cities present certain environmental and psychological challenges, they also offer unmatched resources for health maintenance. Thus, it is overly simplistic to label city life as universally detrimental to health, as it is ultimately a matter of personal choices and how one navigates the urban landscape.
fields.solution:
Task 1:
- Nhóm dữ liệu hợp lý: Chia thành nhóm 'tỷ lệ cao' (Ba Lan, Ý) và 'tỷ lệ thấp' (Hungary, Đức, Đan Mạch) để bài viết có sự phân tích so sánh sâu hơn thay vì liệt kê từng quốc gia.
- Sử dụng từ vựng chỉ mức độ chênh lệch tốt: 'pronounced disparity', 'significant gap', 'lowest performance'.

Task 2:
- Bài viết đạt Band 9.0 nhờ cách phản biện (refutation) thông minh: Thay vì đồng ý hay phản đối hoàn toàn, tác giả chuyển hướng sang 'lối sống của cá nhân' (personal choices). 
- Các luận điểm đều được triển khai theo cấu trúc: Ý chính -> Giải thích -> Ví dụ/Hệ quả, giúp người đọc dễ theo dõi. Từ vựng nâng cao như 'perpetual connectivity', 'sedentary', 'mitigated' làm bài viết chuyên nghiệp.

 PART 1 CLERK: Good morning, ma’am, and welcome to “Australia’s Moving Experience”! How can I help you?
 WOMAN: Well, I... I hope you can help me. I’m so up in the air right now... I...
 CLERK: Just calm down, now. Let me guess: you’re moving and it has you a little confused.
 WOMAN: That’s it exactly. You see, I’m relocating to the United States next month and I’m having a hard time getting organised.
 CLERK: Here, fill out your name and address, and let me ask you a few questions. Oh, what should I call you?
 WOMAN: My name is Jane, Jane Bond . 
 CLERK: OK, Jane, first of all, what’s your work phone number? In case I have any questions about things.
 WOMAN: My work phone is 94635550 . But please try not to call me too often there. My boss hates personal calls.
 CLERK: So does mine, ma’am, so does mine. And what address should we ship your things to?
 WOMAN: My new company is letting me stay temporarily at 509 Clark House , that’s C-L-A-R-K, 1137 University Drive in Seattle.
 CLERK: Seattle? Beautiful city, I hear. Mountains right beside the ocean, almost. Cooler than Australia, too. OK, and when should we come pack your things?
 WOMAN: I guess that would be on Monday , March 11th. 
 CLERK: Do you want any help with an after-packing clean-up? We do that for a small additional charge.
 WOMAN:Yes, that would be helpful. I promised the landlord I’d give her the keys back by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday , the 14th.
 CLERK: Great, we’ll just schedule the clean-up for that day. That way, the place will smell clean and there’ll be no dust.
 WOMAN: Well, you do think of everything! Oh, how much is this going to cost?
 CLERK: Here is a list of our basic prices.
 WOMAN: Oh dear, this seems rather expensive!
 CLERK: Yes ma’am, but you’re paying for the best. We’re careful and we’re fast. Like we say, the only thing we break are speed records getting you moved.
 WOMAN: Well... maybe that’s so... Oh, I nearly forgot to tell you. I don’t want my furniture shipped with me. I won't be looking for an apartment till after I arrive in America. Would it be possible to put my furniture in storage here for a month , then have it sent along later?
 CLERK: Of course, we do that all the time. A couple of other things.
 WOMAN: Here at "A Moving Experience”, we try to pack your things logically. We don’t just throw stuff in boxes.
 CLERK: Do you have any special requests? You know, things you want packed in some special place, so you know where to find them?
 WOMAN: Like what?
 CLERK: Oh, I don’t know... Things like dishes maybe. Not to be rude, but you look like a lady who likes to eat.
 WOMAN: Ahhh! Yes, I need my dishes and things where I can find them quickly.
 CLERK: Great. We'll put those dishes and cutlery in what we call the emergency pack . Can you think of anything else?
 WOMAN: Ummm, I do have an antique tea kettle my great-grandmother gave my mother. I wouldn’t want to lose that. So I guess you’d better put that in storage with the furniture . 
 CLERK: Grandma’s tea kettle with the furniture, got it! Say, how about things like your alarm clock? You don’t want to miss your plane on the big day, right?
 WOMAN: Well, you certainly think of everything! Yes, that’s right. I'll also need my alarm clock where I can find it . 
 CLERK: Fine, we’ll put that in your personal package . And of course, we'll give you a list of where we pack everything. So, all you’ll have to do on Thursday, the 14th is grab your luggage on your way out the door. Um, I couldn’t help noticing the new CD player you’re carrying. Is that a Samsung?
 WOMAN: Why? Yes, it is. One of their best. Cost me nearly a hundred dollars, it did!
 CLERK: Do you want to take special care of it? I mean it’s brand new.
 WOMAN: Take care of it, but nothing special. You can just put it in storage with the furniture .
 CLERK: That looks like everything we need here. I guess you’re all set.
 WOMAN: That was certainly quick. Thank you, young man. This has been a most moving experience!

 PART 2 Good morning everyone, and welcome to the 2nd Annual Wullaballoo Conference on Mastering Computer Languages. I hope you all had a good trip. Before we get underway with today’s programme, let me fill you in as to what’s on tap for tomorrow, Sunday, February 19th.
 At 9:00 a.m. right here in the Main Hall, we’ll be hearing a lecture from Dr John Smith about “ Computer as Teacher ’’. Professor Smith, from the University of Melbourne , is a world-class expert in the field of computer-assisted education, and his talk promises to be both stimulating and informative.
 Immediately afterwards, at 10:30, there will be a presentation of papers by various delegates. That, however, will take place in the Garden Room on the ground floor. If you don’t yet know, the Garden Room is also called the Ballroom, and we’ll be gathering at the west end, the slightly raised area called Level 2. Just look for the crowd. If you get lost, there are signs in the foyer.
 After all that thinking, talking, and listening, I expect everyone will be a bit weary. So at 11:15, there will be a break for coffee, cookies, and other light refreshments. These will be available at the aptly named Refreshment Stand, placed by the door back here in the Main Hall. Also, if you choose to skip the formal lunch, you can buy a packed lunch at the stand for a reasonable price.
 I strongly urge you, however, to join us at the formal lunch. That won’t be till one o’clock sharp, so you have time to stroll about town a bit. We’ll be eating at the Sea View Restaurant. The restaurant is located right here in the hotel, on the top floor . It’s a good dozen flights of stairs, so I suggest you take the lift on the ground floor , eh? If you’re not fond of fish, there is an all-you-can-eat barbecue available as
well. They even offer wallaby meat!
 After lunch, we’ll troop back downstairs to Level 2 in the Ballroom for the presentation of further papers, which will begin at 2:00 p.m. Please try to be on time. I know you’ll be a bit tired after lunch, but the Ballroom echoes so with people coming in late. Thank you in advance.
 Once we’ve heard the papers, we’ll break for afternoon tea at 3:10 p.m. No need to walk. The manager of the refreshment stand has graciously agreed to have tea served in the Ballroom. He’s even promised us some special scones, baked from a recipe of his dear old Scottish grandmother.
 Then, tea being drunk and scones munched, we’ll retire here to the Main Hall for some closing remarks and questions. So, by 5:00 we should have the conference wrapped up. But the fun isn’t over! This is Australia mates! We’ll be flocking to the hotel’s own Palm Lounge on the east side of the foyer for an informal reception. You can relax, mingle with the other delegates, and let your hair down a bit. This will run from 5:10 to 6:10, though you’re free to stay as long as you like. The lounge manager has informed me that, for the duration of the actual reception, you can have all-you-can-drink beer for $20.00 with purchase of an advance ticket.
 And, yes, tickets can be purchased from any conference organiser or at the front desk anytime between now and the start of the reception .
 I suggest you come by tomorrow evening to pick up the tickets since the conference hall only holds 800 people. That way, you can also get your journey planned ahead of time and be sure not to miss this truly memorable conference. If you want cocktails, however, I’m sorry. You’ll have to pay for those at the regular price.
 Oh my goodness! Speaking of paying, I see I forgot to tell you a couple of things. The first is about lunch. The charge for the lunch will be $15.00 for all you delegates . If you have guests with you, the cost is $25.00 for the general public, and $6.50 for children under the age of 10. That’s fifteen dollars each, not total for everyone! Another item is about the lunch menu. I very much urge you to try the fish. I mean, look at the restaurant’s name: Sea View. As the name suggests, it is a famous seafood restaurant . The chef is a Basque from Spain, and he really gets quite put out when people ignore his fish specialties for burgers or barbecue. If fish isn’t your thing though, try the steak - he makes an exquisite Filet mignon topped with bleu cheese and mushrooms.
 Finally, if you’d like to buy a ticket, you can have both lunch and the unlimited beer for $35.00 . I should have mentioned that earlier, but I am a bit forgetful. Maybe I should avoid the beer after the conference, eh?
 Well, I’ve said my bit. Are there any questions?

 PART 3
 Hello... are you Professor Van Diezen?
 Yes, I am. And who might you be?
 Oh! Sorry, my name is Tina. I’m a freshman here. They told me I should ask you for advice in choosing courses.
 Well, that’s part of what I’m here for. Please come in and sit down. Now, what are your questions?
 I, I almost don’t know! Everything is so confusing! Like what is a “specialised course”?
 Oh, easy. A specialised course is one that is compulsory, meaning it's a requirement for your major and regular, so you can’t place out by taking a proficiency exam . 
 That sounds pretty strict. Then what are all these general courses? I seem to have to take so many.
 Nothing to be alarmed over. These are courses open to all students and not directly related to your major. The university offers these general courses to choose so that you can become more well-rounded individuals. For example, I see you’re a Microbiology major. So it might be a good idea to take some literature or history courses so that you can know something besides all science.
 You mean these courses are, like, for fun?
 That might be one way to look at it, but don’t tell the literature professor such a thing. Think of a general course as the opposite of a specified course. A specified course is one that pertains directly to your major.
 So can I take any Microbiology course I want?
 Let’s see. Oh, those courses used to be open to Microbiology students only.
 The good thing is, now it’s open to students on a flexible schedule, so it’s not only for full-time students . So the answer is yes, if you have the instructor’s permission. May I ask you why you chose Microbiology?
 Well, I also like plain old Biology, too. You know, fullsized animals. I might even become a veterinarian. Could I take some Biology classes?
 Well, they are open to full-time students only , which I believe is what you are. I don’t know how a freshman would get along with Microbiology, though. I mean, most of the students presently looking into it are from off-campus. 
 Off-campus?
 Yes, you know, people who use it in their work at hospitals, laboratories, even a police detective. Why did you choose Microbiology, if I may ask? I don’t think you quite answered that.
 Well, eventually I want to be a doctor. At least my dad tells me so.
 If I may say so, young lady, you seem a little uncertain.
 Still, I think that might be a good idea for a career. Of course, if you're thinking about being either a doctor or a vet, you should take some Medical Science classes before you even think of applying to med school.
 Great! What should I take?
 There is one small problem. The new Medical Sciences building is under construction, so there are no experimental facilities available until next year . 
 I’m afraid you'll have to wait. But don’t forget to take those courses at the first opportunity!
 Oh, bummer. Is there any other course you'd recommend for someone like me?
 Well, since you seem to like animals, have you ever thought about looking into Environmental Science? 
 No, I never really thought about it before. Is it worthwhile?
 Quite! In fact, it's the fastest growing subject on this campus. 
 I’m sorry, I couldn’t help noticing the long list of classes you’ve written out there. May I have a look?
 Oh, sure.
 Medical Science, Statistics, Laboratory Techniques, Medicine, Mathematics, Computing. My, my, a bit of everything here.
 Is it too much?
 For your first semester, yes. What I suggest is starting out by taking the compulsory courses . Like we said before, the Medical Science can wait.
 Consider taking that in your sophomore year. I think I’d put off Computing, too.
 I recommend to all freshmen that I talk to get the compulsory Mathematics out of the way as early as possible , so take that one. It’ll be one less difficult course you have to focus on when the science lab opens next year, and you have to catch up on classes like Laboratory Techniques. Your major also requires Statistics so you have to balance two Maths classes, and no doubt you should take that . Otherwise, get your required Medicine course out of the way by taking something theory-based. 
 Oh, of course and your Environmental Science class if you’re interested. The others can wait, though I think Computing is definitely a good idea, even though it’s not required. I see too, on your paper there, you seem to have had high marks on the entrance exam.
 Uhhh, yeah. I guess so.
 Don’t be shy! Have you thought about applying for a scholarship?
 Do they have any? I mean, my dad is always complaining about how much money it costs him.
 In your department, there are actually three full scholarships available. They cover tuition and provide $1,500 cash.
 $1,500 cash?! Party!
 Please, Miss. The money is intended more as a textbook allowance , not party money. If you promise to behave, I’ll show you how to apply.
 Great, and thanks!

 PART 4 We’ve been talking about choosing building materials in the last week. Now, a great many factors influence the choice of building materials. You can’t make a house of cards, right? And “people who live in glass houses...” and all that... Anyhow, today I’d like to say a few words about flooring.
 Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic for instance, which offer mixed blessings when used as a flooring surface. On the one hand, plastic is cheaper than nearly any other alternative, short of bare ground. Plastic also does not warp like wood. On the other hand, the best that can be said about plastic is that it “looks like” wood or stone. However, it cannot replace the real materials. As I have mentioned, I’m fixing up a new house. The decorator my wife hired told me, “Plastic does a great job of looking exactly like plastic.” Besides, it scratches easily, fades or discolours, and starts cracking within a year or two. So, if you’re fitting out a sleazy hotel or plan to live in a trailer park, go with the plastic. Really, though, for all intents and purposes, this leaves us with wood or stone as choices for flooring.
 Stone and wood are alike in at least one respect: both go through processing before they can be put to use. Since few of us cut our own lumber or quarry our own stone, this is not perhaps a pressing concern. Still, do-it-yourselfers would do well to remember to buy only properly seasoned wood. Unseasoned wood warps and a warped floor quickly becomes firewood (and its owner quickly becomes poorer). Likewise, except for dull-hued materials like slate or sandstone, most stone floors are polished before installation. The choice goes well beyond just wood or stone - each type requires many further considerations. A few special remarks are called for when considering wood, for example. As always, aesthetics, personal taste, and layout all play roles as well as the type of house or room. Oh, and certainly don’t forget the cost . When it comes to cost, a rule of thumb is that the softer and less exotic the wood, the lower the cost. In the US, for instance, pine is both ubiquitous and cheap. Mahogany is imported and exorbitantly expensive. If you’re on any kind of budget when remodeling, it’s really helpful to remember to go for the softer woods.
 Aside from cost, there are still lots of different factors that are important in choosing the best flooring for the job. Continuing with the example of wood, one must consider the effects of each type of wood on the mood of the room. When selecting the best wood to use, particular attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns , texture, and colour. In rooms where relaxation or deep thought is the aim - say bedrooms or the
study - dark, strong grained woods are the rule.
 Here the grain ought to match the furniture for a feeling of homogeneity. In rooms where activity and motion are typical - the dining room or living room - lighter, finer- grained lumber is more suitable.
 In such a setting, the wood grain might be useful in offering a contrast to the furniture. This leads to a feel of subconscious excitement, in keeping with the room’s function.
 In either case, though, consult a decorator. It is a decorator’s job to know what materials to use to fit the function of the room. Though some things about putting together a room are subjective and based on one’s individual taste, materials appropriate to a room’s function are much more straightforward. A decorator takes the needs of the customer and uses a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words . Since feelings vary from person to person, verbal descriptions of wood types tend to be ambiguous. You want the wood you select, not something approximate! And if you do decide to do it yourself, remember that all wood must be treated with preservatives to enhance its appearance and preserve its natural beauty.
 In the case of stone, or “quarry tile” as flat-cut flooring stone is properly called, a new set of considerations must be weighed up. Simple colour aside, the degree of reflection must be kept in mind. This is called the “reflectance rate”, which is expressed in a number between 0.0 and 1.0, depending on the amount of light it reflects.
 At one end of the scale is polished silver. At a rating of 1.0, this shiny surface reflects nearly all of the light directed at it. Numbers closer to zero describe materials that absorb more light. Moving down the scale a bit, we see the plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8 , which makes sense. We know that the colour white reflects all other colours while black absorbs all colours, and plastic itself is a relatively
reflective material.
 Materials that are denser and darker have reflectance rates much closer to zero. The quarry tile I mentioned a while ago has a rate of 0.1 . As you may know, quarry tile is generally dark brown and made from clay so it is quite dense. Of course, there is considerable variation among types of quarry tile because of the hue or treatment of the clay during its creation.
 Does anyone have any guesses as to what materials may have a rate of almost 0.0? We can guess most of these materials are black in colour, but plastic, wood, and even stone reflect some light. One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet . The texture produces almost no shine at all.
 Carrara marble, despite its white hue, is actually lower in reflectivity than black onyx! In any case, the fact that tiles vary somewhat should not be forgotten. A highly reflective floor would not be suitable in a library; it would be indispensable in a ballroom (should your home be large enough to feature one). Again, a rule of thumb is that “light means lively”. Since form and material follow function, one should only use the more reflective materials in rooms where the cultivation and expression of energy is important. Bear in mind too that most types of stone cost more than all but the rarest of woods.
 Of course, there is no reason why some rooms of a house should not feature wood floors or other stone tiles. You can even mix the two. A room with wood panels on the walls can have a beautiful stone floor. My bedroom has white birch walls and a light blue slate floor. The place looks like a Russian hunting lodge. Remember, though, go with what feels right for you. Good taste and the “laws” of interior design are the homeowner’s servants, not his master. It’s only beautiful when you decide it is. I mean, you’re the one who lives there, not the decorator, right? OK, are there any questions?

fields.spelling:
Các lỗi chính tả và bẫy phát âm cần lưu ý:
1. Tên riêng và địa chỉ: 'Clark House' (câu 2), 'University Drive' (câu 3) cần viết hoa danh từ riêng. Số điện thoại (94635550) cần nghe nhịp đọc để điền đủ các số.
2. Bẫy số thứ tự và ngày tháng: '14th' (câu 5) và các mốc thời gian như '11:00 am', '3:10 pm' đòi hỏi sự tập trung để không nhầm lẫn các mốc giờ.
3. Từ đồng âm: 'Break' và 'Brake', 'Weight' và 'Wait'. Cần chú ý ngữ cảnh để viết đúng chính tả.
4. Kỹ thuật viết hoa: Các từ chuyên ngành hoặc địa danh như 'Main Gateway', 'Palm Lounge', 'A-Frame', 'River Thames' phải viết hoa đúng quy tắc.
fields.vocab:
1. Relocating (v): Di dời, chuyển nhà
2. Storage (n): Sự lưu kho, kho bãi
3. Delegate (n): Đại biểu tham dự hội nghị
4. Mingle (v): Trò chuyện giao lưu trong sự kiện
5. Specialized course (n phrase): Khóa học chuyên sâu
6. Compulsory (adj): Bắt buộc
7. Seasoned wood (n phrase): Gỗ đã được xử lý khô/tẩm sấy
8. Reflectance rate (n phrase): Chỉ số phản xạ ánh sáng
9. Homogeneity (n): Tính đồng nhất
10. Stratified (adj): Bị phân tầng
fields.transcript:
Phân tích bản ghi âm và chiến thuật nhận diện bẫy nhiễu:
1. Bẫy thời gian làm việc (Part 1): Nhân viên hỏi ngày làm việc, khách hàng đưa ra mốc 11 tháng 3 (đóng gói) và 14 tháng 3 (dọn dẹp). Thí sinh cần điền đúng 'Thursday' cho câu 5 dựa trên thông tin ngày 14.
2. Bẫy địa điểm hội nghị (Part 2): Người thuyết minh đưa ra nhiều địa điểm nhiễu (Main Hall, Garden Room, Ballroom, Palm Lounge). Cần bám sát mốc giờ 1:00 p.m. tại nhà hàng Sea View hoặc reception tại Palm Lounge để không nhầm lẫn vị trí.
3. Bẫy tư vấn học thuật (Part 3): Giáo sư Lee liệt kê hàng loạt tên sách của các tác giả Bayer, Oliver, Billy, Andrew. Cần nghe kỹ thái độ ('worth reading', 'avoid', 'excellent') để khớp đúng với lời khuyên cho từng sinh viên.
4. Bẫy chỉ số kỹ thuật (Part 4): Khi nhắc đến 'reflectance rate' (từ 0.0 đến 1.0), người nghe cần chú ý các số liệu '0.8', '0.1' cho các bề mặt khác nhau. Bẫy nằm ở việc mô tả bề mặt (bạc bóng, nhựa trắng, gạch quarry) để dẫn đến con số tương ứng.
fields.explanation:
Chi tiết đáp án và giải thích nguồn trích xuất dữ liệu:

- Câu 1: 94635550
+ Dẫn chứng: 'My work phone is 94635550.'
+ Giải thích: Số điện thoại công việc của Jane Bond.

- Câu 2: Clark House
+ Dẫn chứng: '...stay temporarily at 509 Clark House...'
+ Giải thích: Địa chỉ tạm trú tại Seattle.

- Câu 3: University Drive
+ Dẫn chứng: '...1137 University Drive in Seattle.'
+ Giải thích: Tên đường tại địa chỉ mới.

- Câu 4: Monday
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Do you want any help with an after-packing clean-up? ... Monday, March 11th.'
+ Giải thích: Ngày bắt đầu đóng gói.

- Câu 5: Thursday
+ Dẫn chứng: '...by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, the 14th.'
+ Giải thích: Hạn chót dọn dẹp là thứ Năm.

- Câu 6: 1 month
+ Dẫn chứng: '...put my furniture in storage here for a month...'
+ Giải thích: Thời gian lưu kho đồ đạc là 1 tháng.

- Câu 11: Computer as Teacher
+ Dẫn chứng: 'lecture from Dr John Smith about “Computer as Teacher”.'
+ Giải thích: Tên bài giảng lúc 9h sáng.

- Câu 12: University of Melbourne
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Professor Smith, from the University of Melbourne...'
+ Giải thích: Đơn vị công tác của diễn giả.

- Câu 13: top floor
+ Dẫn chứng: 'The restaurant is located... on the top floor.'
+ Giải thích: Vị trí nhà hàng ăn trưa.

- Câu 14: ground floor
+ Dẫn chứng: '...so I suggest you take the lift on the ground floor.'
+ Giải thích: Vị trí đặt thang máy.

- Câu 15: 3:10
+ Dẫn chứng: '...afternoon tea at 3:10 p.m.'
+ Giải thích: Giờ nghỉ trà chiều.

- Câu 16: Palm Lounge
+ Dẫn chứng: '...hotel’s own Palm Lounge on the east side...'
+ Giải thích: Nơi diễn ra buổi tiếp đón thân mật.

- Câu 21: 614
+ Dẫn chứng: 'His new room number is 614...'
+ Giải thích: Số phòng mới của Giáo sư.

- Câu 22: 2 o'clock
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I remember our tutorial time is at two o’clock, right?'
+ Giải thích: Thời gian họp nhóm hướng dẫn.

- Câu 23: extend thesis deadline
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I mean I hope to extend my thesis deadline.'
+ Giải thích: Mục đích sinh viên tìm giáo sư.

- Câu 24: reading materials
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I’m having too many reading materials to read.'
+ Giải thích: Khó khăn của sinh viên là quá nhiều tài liệu đọc.

- Câu 31: plastic
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic...'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu nhân tạo được nhắc đến.

- Câu 32: processing
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Stone and wood are alike... both go through processing...'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu cần qua công đoạn xử lý trước khi dùng.

- Câu 33: properly seasoned
+ Dẫn chứng: '...remember to buy only properly seasoned wood.'
+ Giải thích: Gỗ phải được tẩm sấy/xử lý khô đúng cách.

- Câu 34: polished
+ Dẫn chứng: '...most stone floors are polished before installation.'
+ Giải thích: Đá lát sàn cần được đánh bóng.

- Câu 35: cost
+ Dẫn chứng: '...don’t forget the cost.'
+ Giải thích: Yếu tố tài chính quan trọng khi xây dựng.

- Câu 36: grain pattern(s)
+ Dẫn chứng: '...attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns, texture, and colour.'
+ Giải thích: Vân gỗ ảnh hưởng đến tâm trạng căn phòng.

- Câu 37: words
+ Dẫn chứng: '...use a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words.'
+ Giải thích: Dùng công thức toán thay vì mô tả bằng lời chủ quan.

- Câu 38: 0.8
+ Dẫn chứng: '...plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8.'
+ Giải thích: Chỉ số phản xạ của nhựa trắng.

- Câu 39: 0.1
+ Dẫn chứng: 'The quarry tile... has a rate of 0.1.'
+ Giải thích: Chỉ số phản xạ của gạch quarry.

- Câu 40: black velvet
+ Dẫn chứng: 'One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet.'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu có chỉ số phản xạ gần bằng 0.

 PART 1 CLERK: Good morning, ma’am, and welcome to “Australia’s Moving Experience”! How can I help you?
 WOMAN: Well, I... I hope you can help me. I’m so up in the air right now... I...
 CLERK: Just calm down, now. Let me guess: you’re moving and it has you a little confused.
 WOMAN: That’s it exactly. You see, I’m relocating to the United States next month and I’m having a hard time getting organised.
 CLERK: Here, fill out your name and address, and let me ask you a few questions. Oh, what should I call you?
 WOMAN: My name is Jane, Jane Bond . 
 CLERK: OK, Jane, first of all, what’s your work phone number? In case I have any questions about things.
 WOMAN: My work phone is 94635550 . But please try not to call me too often there. My boss hates personal calls.
 CLERK: So does mine, ma’am, so does mine. And what address should we ship your things to?
 WOMAN: My new company is letting me stay temporarily at 509 Clark House , that’s C-L-A-R-K, 1137 University Drive in Seattle.
 CLERK: Seattle? Beautiful city, I hear. Mountains right beside the ocean, almost. Cooler than Australia, too. OK, and when should we come pack your things?
 WOMAN: I guess that would be on Monday , March 11th. 
 CLERK: Do you want any help with an after-packing clean-up? We do that for a small additional charge.
 WOMAN:Yes, that would be helpful. I promised the landlord I’d give her the keys back by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday , the 14th.
 CLERK: Great, we’ll just schedule the clean-up for that day. That way, the place will smell clean and there’ll be no dust.
 WOMAN: Well, you do think of everything! Oh, how much is this going to cost?
 CLERK: Here is a list of our basic prices.
 WOMAN: Oh dear, this seems rather expensive!
 CLERK: Yes ma’am, but you’re paying for the best. We’re careful and we’re fast. Like we say, the only thing we break are speed records getting you moved.
 WOMAN: Well... maybe that’s so... Oh, I nearly forgot to tell you. I don’t want my furniture shipped with me. I won't be looking for an apartment till after I arrive in America. Would it be possible to put my furniture in storage here for a month , then have it sent along later?
 CLERK: Of course, we do that all the time. A couple of other things.
 WOMAN: Here at "A Moving Experience”, we try to pack your things logically. We don’t just throw stuff in boxes.
 CLERK: Do you have any special requests? You know, things you want packed in some special place, so you know where to find them?
 WOMAN: Like what?
 CLERK: Oh, I don’t know... Things like dishes maybe. Not to be rude, but you look like a lady who likes to eat.
 WOMAN: Ahhh! Yes, I need my dishes and things where I can find them quickly.
 CLERK: Great. We'll put those dishes and cutlery in what we call the emergency pack . Can you think of anything else?
 WOMAN: Ummm, I do have an antique tea kettle my great-grandmother gave my mother. I wouldn’t want to lose that. So I guess you’d better put that in storage with the furniture . 
 CLERK: Grandma’s tea kettle with the furniture, got it! Say, how about things like your alarm clock? You don’t want to miss your plane on the big day, right?
 WOMAN: Well, you certainly think of everything! Yes, that’s right. I'll also need my alarm clock where I can find it . 
 CLERK: Fine, we’ll put that in your personal package . And of course, we'll give you a list of where we pack everything. So, all you’ll have to do on Thursday, the 14th is grab your luggage on your way out the door. Um, I couldn’t help noticing the new CD player you’re carrying. Is that a Samsung?
 WOMAN: Why? Yes, it is. One of their best. Cost me nearly a hundred dollars, it did!
 CLERK: Do you want to take special care of it? I mean it’s brand new.
 WOMAN: Take care of it, but nothing special. You can just put it in storage with the furniture .
 CLERK: That looks like everything we need here. I guess you’re all set.
 WOMAN: That was certainly quick. Thank you, young man. This has been a most moving experience!

 PART 2 Good morning everyone, and welcome to the 2nd Annual Wullaballoo Conference on Mastering Computer Languages. I hope you all had a good trip. Before we get underway with today’s programme, let me fill you in as to what’s on tap for tomorrow, Sunday, February 19th.
 At 9:00 a.m. right here in the Main Hall, we’ll be hearing a lecture from Dr John Smith about “ Computer as Teacher ’’. Professor Smith, from the University of Melbourne , is a world-class expert in the field of computer-assisted education, and his talk promises to be both stimulating and informative.
 Immediately afterwards, at 10:30, there will be a presentation of papers by various delegates. That, however, will take place in the Garden Room on the ground floor. If you don’t yet know, the Garden Room is also called the Ballroom, and we’ll be gathering at the west end, the slightly raised area called Level 2. Just look for the crowd. If you get lost, there are signs in the foyer.
 After all that thinking, talking, and listening, I expect everyone will be a bit weary. So at 11:15, there will be a break for coffee, cookies, and other light refreshments. These will be available at the aptly named Refreshment Stand, placed by the door back here in the Main Hall. Also, if you choose to skip the formal lunch, you can buy a packed lunch at the stand for a reasonable price.
 I strongly urge you, however, to join us at the formal lunch. That won’t be till one o’clock sharp, so you have time to stroll about town a bit. We’ll be eating at the Sea View Restaurant. The restaurant is located right here in the hotel, on the top floor . It’s a good dozen flights of stairs, so I suggest you take the lift on the ground floor , eh? If you’re not fond of fish, there is an all-you-can-eat barbecue available as
well. They even offer wallaby meat!
 After lunch, we’ll troop back downstairs to Level 2 in the Ballroom for the presentation of further papers, which will begin at 2:00 p.m. Please try to be on time. I know you’ll be a bit tired after lunch, but the Ballroom echoes so with people coming in late. Thank you in advance.
 Once we’ve heard the papers, we’ll break for afternoon tea at 3:10 p.m. No need to walk. The manager of the refreshment stand has graciously agreed to have tea served in the Ballroom. He’s even promised us some special scones, baked from a recipe of his dear old Scottish grandmother.
 Then, tea being drunk and scones munched, we’ll retire here to the Main Hall for some closing remarks and questions. So, by 5:00 we should have the conference wrapped up. But the fun isn’t over! This is Australia mates! We’ll be flocking to the hotel’s own Palm Lounge on the east side of the foyer for an informal reception. You can relax, mingle with the other delegates, and let your hair down a bit. This will run from 5:10 to 6:10, though you’re free to stay as long as you like. The lounge manager has informed me that, for the duration of the actual reception, you can have all-you-can-drink beer for $20.00 with purchase of an advance ticket.
 And, yes, tickets can be purchased from any conference organiser or at the front desk anytime between now and the start of the reception .
 I suggest you come by tomorrow evening to pick up the tickets since the conference hall only holds 800 people. That way, you can also get your journey planned ahead of time and be sure not to miss this truly memorable conference. If you want cocktails, however, I’m sorry. You’ll have to pay for those at the regular price.
 Oh my goodness! Speaking of paying, I see I forgot to tell you a couple of things. The first is about lunch. The charge for the lunch will be $15.00 for all you delegates . If you have guests with you, the cost is $25.00 for the general public, and $6.50 for children under the age of 10. That’s fifteen dollars each, not total for everyone! Another item is about the lunch menu. I very much urge you to try the fish. I mean, look at the restaurant’s name: Sea View. As the name suggests, it is a famous seafood restaurant . The chef is a Basque from Spain, and he really gets quite put out when people ignore his fish specialties for burgers or barbecue. If fish isn’t your thing though, try the steak - he makes an exquisite Filet mignon topped with bleu cheese and mushrooms.
 Finally, if you’d like to buy a ticket, you can have both lunch and the unlimited beer for $35.00 . I should have mentioned that earlier, but I am a bit forgetful. Maybe I should avoid the beer after the conference, eh?
 Well, I’ve said my bit. Are there any questions?

 PART 3
 Hello... are you Professor Van Diezen?
 Yes, I am. And who might you be?
 Oh! Sorry, my name is Tina. I’m a freshman here. They told me I should ask you for advice in choosing courses.
 Well, that’s part of what I’m here for. Please come in and sit down. Now, what are your questions?
 I, I almost don’t know! Everything is so confusing! Like what is a “specialised course”?
 Oh, easy. A specialised course is one that is compulsory, meaning it's a requirement for your major and regular, so you can’t place out by taking a proficiency exam . 
 That sounds pretty strict. Then what are all these general courses? I seem to have to take so many.
 Nothing to be alarmed over. These are courses open to all students and not directly related to your major. The university offers these general courses to choose so that you can become more well-rounded individuals. For example, I see you’re a Microbiology major. So it might be a good idea to take some literature or history courses so that you can know something besides all science.
 You mean these courses are, like, for fun?
 That might be one way to look at it, but don’t tell the literature professor such a thing. Think of a general course as the opposite of a specified course. A specified course is one that pertains directly to your major.
 So can I take any Microbiology course I want?
 Let’s see. Oh, those courses used to be open to Microbiology students only.
 The good thing is, now it’s open to students on a flexible schedule, so it’s not only for full-time students . So the answer is yes, if you have the instructor’s permission. May I ask you why you chose Microbiology?
 Well, I also like plain old Biology, too. You know, fullsized animals. I might even become a veterinarian. Could I take some Biology classes?
 Well, they are open to full-time students only , which I believe is what you are. I don’t know how a freshman would get along with Microbiology, though. I mean, most of the students presently looking into it are from off-campus. 
 Off-campus?
 Yes, you know, people who use it in their work at hospitals, laboratories, even a police detective. Why did you choose Microbiology, if I may ask? I don’t think you quite answered that.
 Well, eventually I want to be a doctor. At least my dad tells me so.
 If I may say so, young lady, you seem a little uncertain.
 Still, I think that might be a good idea for a career. Of course, if you're thinking about being either a doctor or a vet, you should take some Medical Science classes before you even think of applying to med school.
 Great! What should I take?
 There is one small problem. The new Medical Sciences building is under construction, so there are no experimental facilities available until next year . 
 I’m afraid you'll have to wait. But don’t forget to take those courses at the first opportunity!
 Oh, bummer. Is there any other course you'd recommend for someone like me?
 Well, since you seem to like animals, have you ever thought about looking into Environmental Science? 
 No, I never really thought about it before. Is it worthwhile?
 Quite! In fact, it's the fastest growing subject on this campus. 
 I’m sorry, I couldn’t help noticing the long list of classes you’ve written out there. May I have a look?
 Oh, sure.
 Medical Science, Statistics, Laboratory Techniques, Medicine, Mathematics, Computing. My, my, a bit of everything here.
 Is it too much?
 For your first semester, yes. What I suggest is starting out by taking the compulsory courses . Like we said before, the Medical Science can wait.
 Consider taking that in your sophomore year. I think I’d put off Computing, too.
 I recommend to all freshmen that I talk to get the compulsory Mathematics out of the way as early as possible , so take that one. It’ll be one less difficult course you have to focus on when the science lab opens next year, and you have to catch up on classes like Laboratory Techniques. Your major also requires Statistics so you have to balance two Maths classes, and no doubt you should take that . Otherwise, get your required Medicine course out of the way by taking something theory-based. 
 Oh, of course and your Environmental Science class if you’re interested. The others can wait, though I think Computing is definitely a good idea, even though it’s not required. I see too, on your paper there, you seem to have had high marks on the entrance exam.
 Uhhh, yeah. I guess so.
 Don’t be shy! Have you thought about applying for a scholarship?
 Do they have any? I mean, my dad is always complaining about how much money it costs him.
 In your department, there are actually three full scholarships available. They cover tuition and provide $1,500 cash.
 $1,500 cash?! Party!
 Please, Miss. The money is intended more as a textbook allowance , not party money. If you promise to behave, I’ll show you how to apply.
 Great, and thanks!

 PART 4 We’ve been talking about choosing building materials in the last week. Now, a great many factors influence the choice of building materials. You can’t make a house of cards, right? And “people who live in glass houses...” and all that... Anyhow, today I’d like to say a few words about flooring.
 Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic for instance, which offer mixed blessings when used as a flooring surface. On the one hand, plastic is cheaper than nearly any other alternative, short of bare ground. Plastic also does not warp like wood. On the other hand, the best that can be said about plastic is that it “looks like” wood or stone. However, it cannot replace the real materials. As I have mentioned, I’m fixing up a new house. The decorator my wife hired told me, “Plastic does a great job of looking exactly like plastic.” Besides, it scratches easily, fades or discolours, and starts cracking within a year or two. So, if you’re fitting out a sleazy hotel or plan to live in a trailer park, go with the plastic. Really, though, for all intents and purposes, this leaves us with wood or stone as choices for flooring.
 Stone and wood are alike in at least one respect: both go through processing before they can be put to use. Since few of us cut our own lumber or quarry our own stone, this is not perhaps a pressing concern. Still, do-it-yourselfers would do well to remember to buy only properly seasoned wood. Unseasoned wood warps and a warped floor quickly becomes firewood (and its owner quickly becomes poorer). Likewise, except for dull-hued materials like slate or sandstone, most stone floors are polished before installation. The choice goes well beyond just wood or stone - each type requires many further considerations. A few special remarks are called for when considering wood, for example. As always, aesthetics, personal taste, and layout all play roles as well as the type of house or room. Oh, and certainly don’t forget the cost . When it comes to cost, a rule of thumb is that the softer and less exotic the wood, the lower the cost. In the US, for instance, pine is both ubiquitous and cheap. Mahogany is imported and exorbitantly expensive. If you’re on any kind of budget when remodeling, it’s really helpful to remember to go for the softer woods.
 Aside from cost, there are still lots of different factors that are important in choosing the best flooring for the job. Continuing with the example of wood, one must consider the effects of each type of wood on the mood of the room. When selecting the best wood to use, particular attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns , texture, and colour. In rooms where relaxation or deep thought is the aim - say bedrooms or the
study - dark, strong grained woods are the rule.
 Here the grain ought to match the furniture for a feeling of homogeneity. In rooms where activity and motion are typical - the dining room or living room - lighter, finer- grained lumber is more suitable.
 In such a setting, the wood grain might be useful in offering a contrast to the furniture. This leads to a feel of subconscious excitement, in keeping with the room’s function.
 In either case, though, consult a decorator. It is a decorator’s job to know what materials to use to fit the function of the room. Though some things about putting together a room are subjective and based on one’s individual taste, materials appropriate to a room’s function are much more straightforward. A decorator takes the needs of the customer and uses a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words . Since feelings vary from person to person, verbal descriptions of wood types tend to be ambiguous. You want the wood you select, not something approximate! And if you do decide to do it yourself, remember that all wood must be treated with preservatives to enhance its appearance and preserve its natural beauty.
 In the case of stone, or “quarry tile” as flat-cut flooring stone is properly called, a new set of considerations must be weighed up. Simple colour aside, the degree of reflection must be kept in mind. This is called the “reflectance rate”, which is expressed in a number between 0.0 and 1.0, depending on the amount of light it reflects.
 At one end of the scale is polished silver. At a rating of 1.0, this shiny surface reflects nearly all of the light directed at it. Numbers closer to zero describe materials that absorb more light. Moving down the scale a bit, we see the plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8 , which makes sense. We know that the colour white reflects all other colours while black absorbs all colours, and plastic itself is a relatively
reflective material.
 Materials that are denser and darker have reflectance rates much closer to zero. The quarry tile I mentioned a while ago has a rate of 0.1 . As you may know, quarry tile is generally dark brown and made from clay so it is quite dense. Of course, there is considerable variation among types of quarry tile because of the hue or treatment of the clay during its creation.
 Does anyone have any guesses as to what materials may have a rate of almost 0.0? We can guess most of these materials are black in colour, but plastic, wood, and even stone reflect some light. One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet . The texture produces almost no shine at all.
 Carrara marble, despite its white hue, is actually lower in reflectivity than black onyx! In any case, the fact that tiles vary somewhat should not be forgotten. A highly reflective floor would not be suitable in a library; it would be indispensable in a ballroom (should your home be large enough to feature one). Again, a rule of thumb is that “light means lively”. Since form and material follow function, one should only use the more reflective materials in rooms where the cultivation and expression of energy is important. Bear in mind too that most types of stone cost more than all but the rarest of woods.
 Of course, there is no reason why some rooms of a house should not feature wood floors or other stone tiles. You can even mix the two. A room with wood panels on the walls can have a beautiful stone floor. My bedroom has white birch walls and a light blue slate floor. The place looks like a Russian hunting lodge. Remember, though, go with what feels right for you. Good taste and the “laws” of interior design are the homeowner’s servants, not his master. It’s only beautiful when you decide it is. Phân tích bản ghi âm và chiến thuật nhận diện bẫy nhiễu:
1. Bẫy thời gian làm việc (Part 1): Nhân viên hỏi ngày làm việc, khách hàng đưa ra mốc 11 tháng 3 (đóng gói) và 14 tháng 3 (dọn dẹp). Thí sinh cần điền đúng 'Thursday' cho câu 5 dựa trên thông tin ngày 14.
2. Bẫy địa điểm hội nghị (Part 2): Người thuyết minh đưa ra nhiều địa điểm nhiễu (Main Hall, Garden Room, Ballroom, Palm Lounge). Cần bám sát mốc giờ 1:00 p.m. tại nhà hàng Sea View hoặc reception tại Palm Lounge để không nhầm lẫn vị trí.
3. Bẫy tư vấn học thuật (Part 3): Giáo sư Lee liệt kê hàng loạt tên sách của các tác giả Bayer, Oliver, Billy, Andrew. Cần nghe kỹ thái độ ('worth reading', 'avoid', 'excellent') để khớp đúng với lời khuyên cho từng sinh viên.
4. Bẫy chỉ số kỹ thuật (Part 4): Khi nhắc đến 'reflectance rate' (từ 0.0 đến 1.0), người nghe cần chú ý các số liệu '0.8', '0.1' cho các bề mặt khác nhau. Bẫy nằm ở việc mô tả bề mặt (bạc bóng, nhựa trắng, gạch quarry) để dẫn đến con số tương ứng.
fields.explanation:
Chi tiết đáp án và giải thích nguồn trích xuất dữ liệu từ Transcript:

- Câu 1: 94635550
+ Dẫn chứng: 'My work phone is 94635550.'
+ Giải thích: Số điện thoại công việc của Jane Bond.

- Câu 2: Clark House
+ Dẫn chứng: '...stay temporarily at 509 Clark House...'
+ Giải thích: Địa chỉ tạm trú tại Seattle.

- Câu 3: University Drive
+ Dẫn chứng: '...1137 University Drive in Seattle.'
+ Giải thích: Tên đường tại địa chỉ mới.

- Câu 4: Monday
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Do you want any help with an after-packing clean-up? ... Monday, March 11th.'
+ Giải thích: Ngày bắt đầu đóng gói.

- Câu 5: Thursday
+ Dẫn chứng: '...by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, the 14th.'
+ Giải thích: Hạn chót dọn dẹp là thứ Năm.

- Câu 6: 1 month
+ Dẫn chứng: '...put my furniture in storage here for a month...'
+ Giải thích: Thời gian lưu kho đồ đạc là 1 tháng.

- Câu 11: Computer as Teacher
+ Dẫn chứng: 'lecture from Dr John Smith about “Computer as Teacher”.'
+ Giải thích: Tên bài giảng lúc 9h sáng.

- Câu 12: University of Melbourne
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Professor Smith, from the University of Melbourne...'
+ Giải thích: Đơn vị công tác của diễn giả.

- Câu 13: top floor
+ Dẫn chứng: 'The restaurant is located... on the top floor.'
+ Giải thích: Vị trí nhà hàng ăn trưa.

- Câu 14: ground floor
+ Dẫn chứng: '...so I suggest you take the lift on the ground floor.'
+ Giải thích: Vị trí đặt thang máy.

- Câu 15: 3:10
+ Dẫn chứng: '...afternoon tea at 3:10 p.m.'
+ Giải thích: Giờ nghỉ trà chiều.

- Câu 16: Palm Lounge
+ Dẫn chứng: '...hotel’s own Palm Lounge on the east side...'
+ Giải thích: Nơi diễn ra buổi tiếp đón thân mật.

- Câu 21: 614
+ Dẫn chứng: 'His new room number is 614...'
+ Giải thích: Số phòng mới của Giáo sư.

- Câu 22: 2 o'clock
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I remember our tutorial time is at two o’clock, right?'
+ Giải thích: Thời gian họp nhóm hướng dẫn.

- Câu 23: extend thesis deadline
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I mean I hope to extend my thesis deadline.'
+ Giải thích: Mục đích sinh viên tìm giáo sư.

- Câu 24: reading materials
+ Dẫn chứng: 'I’m having too many reading materials to read.'
+ Giải thích: Khó khăn của sinh viên là quá nhiều tài liệu đọc.

- Câu 31: plastic
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic...'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu nhân tạo được nhắc đến.

- Câu 32: processing
+ Dẫn chứng: 'Stone and wood are alike... both go through processing...'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu cần qua công đoạn xử lý trước khi dùng.

- Câu 33: properly seasoned
+ Dẫn chứng: '...remember to buy only properly seasoned wood.'
+ Giải thích: Gỗ phải được tẩm sấy/xử lý khô đúng cách.

- Câu 34: polished
+ Dẫn chứng: '...most stone floors are polished before installation.'
+ Giải thích: Đá lát sàn cần được đánh bóng.

- Câu 35: cost
+ Dẫn chứng: '...don’t forget the cost.'
+ Giải thích: Yếu tố tài chính quan trọng khi xây dựng.

- Câu 36: grain pattern(s)
+ Dẫn chứng: '...attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns, texture, and colour.'
+ Giải thích: Vân gỗ ảnh hưởng đến tâm trạng căn phòng.

- Câu 37: words
+ Dẫn chứng: '...use a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words.'
+ Giải thích: Dùng công thức toán thay vì mô tả bằng lời chủ quan.

- Câu 38: 0.8
+ Dẫn chứng: '...plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8.'
+ Giải thích: Chỉ số phản xạ của nhựa trắng.

- Câu 39: 0.1
+ Dẫn chứng: 'The quarry tile... has a rate of 0.1.'
+ Giải thích: Chỉ số phản xạ của gạch quarry.

- Câu 40: black velvet
+ Dẫn chứng: 'One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet.'
+ Giải thích: Vật liệu có chỉ số phản xạ gần bằng 0.

- Dạng biểu đồ: Biểu đồ tròn (Pie charts) so sánh tỷ lệ phần trăm theo hai mốc thời gian (1985 và hiện nay).

fields.ideas:
Task 1:
- Overview: Cơ cấu khóa học đã thay đổi mạnh mẽ, với sự chuyển dịch sang công nghệ thông tin (IT) và giảm sự quan tâm đến ngoại ngữ và nghệ thuật truyền thống.
- Body 1: Các khóa học truyền thống như Modern languages (24% -> 17%) và Art (17% -> 15%) giảm. Music appreciation (8%) đã biến mất hoàn toàn.
- Body 2: Các khóa học kỹ năng thực tế như Cookery (14% -> 19%) tăng. IT (27%) trở thành khóa học phổ biến nhất thay thế hoàn toàn vị trí của các khóa học bị loại bỏ. Fitness and dance ổn định ở mức 22%. 

Task 2:
- Introduction: Khẳng định tiền bạc là yếu tố quan trọng nhưng không phải là duy nhất. Tuyên bố lập trường: Đồng ý một phần (Disagree with the implication that money is the 'only' reason).
- Body 1 (Tiền bạc): Nhu cầu cơ bản (thức ăn, nhà ở), mong muốn nâng cao mức sống, sự an toàn tài chính cho gia đình.
- Body 2 (Động lực khác): Đam mê (passion), sự công nhận từ xã hội (social recognition), sự phát triển bản thân (self-development), đóng góp cho cộng đồng (altruism).
- Conclusion: Tiền là điều kiện cần để tồn tại, nhưng niềm vui và ý nghĩa công việc là điều kiện đủ để con người gắn bó bền lâu.
fields.sample:
Task 1:
The two pie charts compare the preferences of students attending an adult education centre in 1985 and this year, highlighting a shift in the popularity of various courses.

Overall, the most striking change is the emergence of Information Technology as a dominant course, alongside a decline in traditional subjects such as modern languages and arts. Fitness and dance remained the only constant, maintaining an identical share throughout both periods.

In 1985, modern languages were the most favored course, accounting for 24% of all enrollments. This was closely followed by fitness and dance at 22% and art at 17%. Local history and cookery comprised 15% and 14% of the student base, respectively, while music appreciation was the least popular, at 8%.

By this year, the landscape had shifted considerably. IT, which was non-existent in the 1985 curriculum, became the most sought-after subject, attracting 27% of students. Simultaneously, the demand for cookery rose to 19%. In contrast, the popularity of modern languages dropped to 17%, and art decreased to 15%. Local history also saw a slight decline, falling to 12% of total interest, while music appreciation had disappeared entirely from the centre's offerings. Fitness and dance continued to attract exactly 22% of the student body, remaining the most consistent preference.


Task 2:
It is often asserted that the primary driver for industriousness in the workplace is the pursuit of financial reward. While I acknowledge that money is a fundamental motivator due to the necessities of survival and the desire for comfort, I disagree that it is the sole or even the primary reason individuals commit themselves to hard work. Personal growth, passion, and the need for social belonging play equally vital roles in professional motivation.

Admittedly, for a significant portion of the global population, the fundamental need to earn a living remains the main impetus for working hard. In an era of rising living costs, financial stability is a prerequisite for security. Individuals are driven to excel in their roles to secure promotions, salary increments, and bonuses, which in turn allow them to provide for their families and plan for the future. Without this financial incentive, many individuals would find it difficult to maintain the discipline required for a demanding professional life.

However, to reduce human effort to a mere quest for currency is to ignore the human psychological need for purpose. Many professionals, once their basic financial needs are satisfied, continue to work hard due to intrinsic motivations. A surgeon, for example, may put in long hours not merely for a paycheck, but out of a genuine desire to save lives and refine their clinical skills. Similarly, artists, writers, and software developers often labor for hours over creative projects, driven by the satisfaction of producing high-quality work. This need for 'self-actualization' is a powerful engine of productivity that financial compensation alone cannot trigger.

Furthermore, work serves as a crucial social anchor. It provides individuals with a sense of identity, belonging, and community. Many employees are motivated by the camaraderie of their colleagues and the prestige associated with their professional status. This social aspect of work often creates a sense of accountability and pride that keeps individuals dedicated, even in roles that might not be exceptionally well-paid.

In conclusion, while money is a crucial and undeniable factor in why people work hard, it is not the only reason. Hard work is a complex manifestation of our need to survive, our quest for mastery, and our desire for meaningful social connection. Attributing our industriousness purely to financial gain overlooks the profound human desire to make a contribution and fulfill one's potential.
fields.solution:
Task 1:
- Bài mẫu đạt Band 9.0 nhờ khả năng so sánh: Không chỉ liệt kê số liệu mà còn làm nổi bật được sự xuất hiện của IT và sự biến mất của Music appreciation. 
- Cách dùng cụm từ 'non-existent' và 'disappeared entirely' giúp người đọc nắm bắt nhanh những thay đổi mang tính hệ thống.

Task 2:
- Bài viết đạt Band 9.0 nhờ cấu trúc lập luận cân bằng. Tác giả đã công nhận tầm quan trọng của tiền bạc (thực tế) nhưng nâng cấp bài viết bằng các luận điểm về tâm lý học ('intrinsic motivation', 'self-actualization'). 
- Việc sử dụng ví dụ (bác sĩ, nghệ sĩ) giúp bài viết cụ thể và có tính thuyết phục cao. Ngôn ngữ trang trọng, mạch lạc, không lặp từ.
