 Part 1 READING PASSAGE 1 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1-13 , which are based on Reading Passage 1 below. 

 Hello Happiness!
 Ask 100 people what would make them happy, and a sizeable majority would say “winning the lottery.” Yet, if they won a vast fortune, within a year they would be back to their previous level of happiness. The fact is that money has many uses, but more money does not mean more happiness. Surveys carried out in recent years by leading psychologists and sociologists all confirm that while individuals may increase their material wealth during the course of their lifetime, this has no bearing on their well-being. And what is true for individuals can be applied on a larger scale to the world population. Statistically, wealthier nations do not achieve higher scores on the happiness-ometer than developing or underdeveloped nations. Once the basic criteria of adequate shelter and nutrition are satisfied, increased wealth plays no significant role. So why the obsession with getting rich? The answer, say researchers, is simple. Call it jealousy, competitiveness, or just keeping up with the Joneses, however well we are doing, there is always someone else who is doing better. Just as we acquire a new $25,000 car, our neighbour parks his brand spanking new $40,000 set of wheels in his drive, causing us much consternation, but fuelling us with new aspirations in the process. And so the cycle continues. Money, or material wealth, may be a prime mover, but it is not the foundation of our well-being.
 If money isn’t the key to happiness, then what is? In all 44 countries surveyed by a prominent research centre, family life provided the greatest source of satisfaction. Married people live on average three years longer and enjoy greater physical and psychological health than the unmarried and, surprisingly, couples in a cohabitational relationship. Having a family enhances well-being, and spending more time with one’s family helps even more. Social interaction among families, neighbourhoods, workplaces, communities and religious groups correlates strongly with subjective well-being. In fact, the degree of individuals’ social connections is the best benchmark of their happiness.
 Friendship is another major factor. Indeed, to return to the dollar-equals-happiness equation, in one survey, having a friend converted into $50,000 worth of happiness, and confirms the well-known phenomenon that loneliness can lead to depression. Work is another area central to well-being, and certain features correlate highly with happiness. These include autonomy over how, where, and at what pace work is done, trust between employer and employee, fair treatment, and active participation in the making of decisions. Occupationally, happiness tends to be more common among professionals and managers, that is, people who are in control of the work they do, rather than subservient to their bosses, inequality implies less control for those who are in the weaker position, although there are more risks of losing their privileges for those in the stronger position.
 Control of one’s life in general is also key. Happiness is clearly correlated with the presence of favourable events such as promotion or marriage, and the absence of troubles or bad luck such as accidents, being laid off or conflicts. These events on their own signal the success or failure to reach one’s goals, and therefore the control one has. On a national level, the more that governments recognise individual preferences, the happier their citizens will be. Choice, and citizens’ belief that they can affect the political process, increase subjective well-being. Furthermore, evidence exists for an association between unhappiness and poor health: people from underdeveloped countries are among the unhappiest in the world, and their life expectancy has been falling steadily. People are more satisfied in societies which minimally restrict their freedom of action, in other words, where they are in control rather than being controlled. Happy people are characterised by the belief that they are able to control their situation, whereas unhappy people tend to believe that they are a victim of fate. Happy people are also more psychologically resilient, assertive and open to experience.
 But how good is the evidence for this alternative viewpoint then - that happiness, and not financial status, contributes to good health, and long life? A study of nuns, spanning seven decades, supports this theory. Autobiographies written by the nuns in their early 1920s were scored for positive and negative emotions. Nuns expressing the most positive emotions lived on average ten years longer than those expressing the least positive emotions. Happy people, it seems, are much less likely to fall ill and die than unhappy people.
 But what must we do to be happy? Experts cite the old maxim “be happy with what you’ve got.” Look around you, they say, and identify the positive factors in your life. Concentrating on the negative aspects of one’s life is a no-no, and so is worrying. Worrying is a negative thinking habit that is nearly always about something that lies in the future. It stems, apparently, from our cave dwelling days, when we had to think on a day-to-day basis about how and where to find food and warmth, for example. But in the modern world, worrying simply undermines our ability to enjoy life in the present. More often than not, the things we worry about never come to pass anyway. Just as important is not to dwell on the past - past mistakes, bad experiences, missed opportunities and so on.
 What else can we do? Well, engage in a loving relationship with another adult, and work hard to sustain it. Try to plan frequent interactions with your family, friends and neighbours (in that order). Make sure you’re not working so hard that you’ve no time left for personal relationships and leisure. If you are, leave your job voluntarily to become self-employed, but don’t get sacked — that’s more damaging to well-being than the loss of a spouse, and its effects last longer. In your spare time, join a club, volunteer for community service, or take up religion.
 If none of the above works, then vote for a political party with the same agenda as the King of Bhutan, who announced that his nation’s objective is national happiness.

 Part 2 READING PASSAGE 2 You should, spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14 - 26 , which are based on Reading Passage 2 below. 

 One Who Hopes
 A 
 Language lovers, just like music lovers, enjoy variety. For the latter there's Mozart, The Rolling Stones and Beyonce. For the former there's English, French, Swahili, Urdu... the list is endless. But what about those poor overworked students who find learning difficult, confusing languages a drudge? Wouldn't it put a smile on their faces if there were just one simple, easy-to-learn tongue that would cut their study time by years? Well, of course, it exists. It's called Esperanto, and it's been around for more than 120 years. Esperanto is the most widely spoken artificially constructed international language. The name derives from Doktoro Esperanto, the pseudonym under which L. L. Zamenhof first published his Unua Libro in 1887. The phrase itself means 'one who hopes'. Zamenhof's goal was to create an easy and flexible language as a universal second language to promote peace and international understanding.
 B 
 Zamenhof, after ten years of developing his brainchild from the late 1870s to the early 1880s, had the first Esperanto grammar published in Warsaw in July 1887. The number of speakers grew rapidly over the next few decades, at first primarily in the Russian empire and Eastern Europe, then in Western Europe and the Americas, China, and Japan. In the early years, speakers of Esperanto kept in contact primarily through correspondence and periodicals, but since 1905 world congresses have been held on five continents every year except during the two World Wars. Latest estimates for the numbers of Esperanto speakers are around 2 million. Put in percentage terms, that's about 0.03% of the world's population - no staggering figure, comparatively speaking. One reason is that Esperanto has no official status in any country, but it is an optional subject on the curriculum of several state education systems. It is widely estimated that it can be learned in anywhere between a quarter to a twentieth of the time required for other languages.
 C 
 As a constructed language, Esperanto is not genealogically related to any ethnic language. Whilst it is described as 'a language lexically predominantly Romanic', the phonology, grammar, vocabulary, and semantics are based on the western Indo-European languages. For those of us who are not naturally predisposed to tucking languages under our belts, it is an easy language to learn. It has 5 vowels and 23 consonants. It has one simple way of conjugating all of its verbs. Words are often made from many other roots, making the number of words which one must memorise much smaller. The language is phonetic, and the rules of pronunciation are very simple, so that everyone knows how to pronounce a written word and vice-versa, and word order follows a standard, logical pattern. Through prefixing and suffixing, Esperanto makes it easy to identify words as nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, direct objects and so on, by means of easy-to-spot endings. All this makes for easy language learning. What's more, several research studies demonstrate that studying Esperanto before another foreign language speeds up and improves the learning of the other language. This is presumably because learning subsequent foreign languages is easier than learning one's first, while the use of a grammatically simple and culturally flexible language like Esperanto softens the blow of learning one's first foreign language. In one study, a group of European high school students studied Esperanto for one year, then French for three years, and ended up with a significantly better command of French than a control group who had studied French for all four years.
 D 
 Needless to say, the language has its critics. Some point to the Eastern European features of the language as being harsh and difficult to pronounce, and argue that Esperanto has an artificial feel to it, without the flow of a natural tongue, and that by nature of its artificiality, it is impossible to become emotionally involved with the language. Others cite its lack of cultural history, indigenous literature - "no one has ever written a novel straight into Esperanto" - together with its minimal vocabulary and its inability to express all the necessary philosophical, emotional and psychological concepts.
 E 
 The champions of Esperanto - Esperantists - disagree. They claim that it is a language in which a great body of world literature has appeared in translation: in poetry, novels, literary journals, and, to rebut the accusation that it is not a 'real' language, point out that it is frequently used at international meetings which draw hundreds and thousands of participants. Moreover, on an international scale, it is most useful - and fair - for neutral communication. That means that communication through Esperanto does not give advantages to the members of any particular people or culture, but provides an ethos of equality of rights, tolerance and true internationalism.
 F 
 Esperantists further claim that Esperanto has the potential - were it universally taught for a year or two throughout the world - to empower ordinary people to communicate effectively worldwide on a scale that far exceeds that which is attainable today by only the most linguistically brilliant among us. It offers the opportunity to improve communication in business, diplomacy, scholarship and other fields so that those who speak many different native languages will be able to participate fluently in international conferences and chat comfortably with each other after the formal presentations are made. Nowadays that privilege is often restricted to native speakers of English and those who have special talents and opportunities for learning English as a foreign language.
 G 
 What Esperanto does offer in concrete terms is the potential of saving billions of dollars which are now being spent on translators and interpreters, billions which would be freed up to serve the purposes of governments and organisations that spend so much of their resources to change words from one language into the words of others. Take, for example, the enormously costly conferences, meetings and documentation involved in the European Union parliamentary and administrative procedures - all funded, essentially, by tax payers. And instead of the World Health Organisation, and all NGOs for that matter, devoting enormous sums to provide interpreters and translations, they would be able to devote those huge amounts of money to improving the health of stricken populations throughout the world.

 Part 3 READING PASSAGE 3 You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27 - 40 , which are based on Reading Passage 3 below. 

 LONG-TERM FORECAST: HOT AND DRY
 A 
 Melting land ice in the Arctic is set to cause a global rise in sea levels, leading to disastrous effects for both man and wildlife. Many species worldwide are threatened with extinction, and low-lying islands and land masses will disappear entirely. But the havoc wreaked by the effect of greenhouse gases won’t be confined to just too much water, but the absence of it, as well. In other words, desertification. A decrease in the total amount of rainfall in arid and semi-arid areas could increase the total area of drylands worldwide, and thus the total amount of land potentially at risk from desertification.
 B 
 Desertification is officially recognised as land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas resulting from various factors including climatic variations and human activities. This degradation of formerly productive land is a complex process. It involves multiple causes, and it proceeds at varying rates in different climates. Desertification may intensify a general climatic trend, or initiate a change in local climate, both leading towards greater aridity. The more arid conditions associated with desertification accelerate the depletion of vegetation and soils. Land degradation occurs all over the world, but it is only referred to as desertification when it takes place in drylands. This is because these areas are especially prone to more permanent damage as different areas of degraded land spread and merge together to form desert-like conditions.
 C 
 Global warming brought about by increasing greenhouse gas levels in the atmosphere is expected to increase the variability of weather conditions and extreme events. Many dryland areas face increasingly low and erratic rainfalls, coupled with soil erosion by wind and the drying-up of water resources through increased regional temperatures. Deforestation can also reduce rainfall in certain areas, increasing the threat of desertification. It is not yet possible, despite sophisticated technology, to identify with an acceptable degree of reliability those parts of the Earth where desertification will occur. Existing drylands, which cover over 40% of the total land area of the world, most significantly in Africa and Asia, will probably be most at risk from climate change. These areas already experience low rainfall, and any that falls is usually in the form of short, erratic, high-intensity storms. In addition, such areas also suffer from land degradation due to over-cultivation, overgrazing, deforestation and poor irrigation practices.
 D 
 It is a misconception that droughts cause desertification. Droughts are common in arid and semi-arid lands. Well-managed lands can recover from drought when the rains return. Continued land abuse during droughts, however, increases land degradation. Nor does desertification occur in linear, easily definable patterns. Deserts advance erratically, forming patches on their borders. Areas far from natural deserts can degrade quickly to barren soil, rock, or sand through poor land management. The presence of a nearby desert has no direct relationship to desertification. Unfortunately, an area undergoing desertification is brought to public attention only after the process is well underway. Often little or no data are available to indicate the previous state of the ecosystem or the rate of degradation. Scientists still question whether desertification, as a process of global change, is permanent or how and when it can be halted or reversed.
 E 
 But desertification will not be limited to the drylands of Africa and Asia. According to the environmental organisation Greenpeace, the Mediterranean will suffer substantially, too. If current trends in emissions of greenhouse gases continue, global temperatures are expected to rise faster over the next century than over any time during the last 10,000 years. Significant uncertainties surround predictions of regional climate changes, but it is likely that the Mediterranean region will also warm significantly, increasing the frequency and severity of droughts across the region. As the world warms, global sea levels will rise as oceans expand and glaciers melt. Around much of the Mediterranean basin, sea levels could rise by close to 1m by 2100. As a result, some low-lying coastal areas would be lost through flooding or erosion, while rivers and coastal aquifers would become more salty. The worst affected areas will be the Nile Delta, Venice in Italy and Thessaloniki in Greece, two major cities where local subsidence means that sea levels could rise by at least one-and-a-half times as much as elsewhere.
 F 
 The consequences of all this, says Greenpeace, are far-reaching, and the picture is a gloomy one. Livestock production would suffer due to a deterioration in the quality of rangeland. Yields of grains and other crops could decrease substantially across the Mediterranean region due to increased frequency of drought. Crop production would be further threatened by increases in competition for water and the prevalence of pests and diseases and land loss through desertification and sea-level rise. The combination of heat and pollution would lead to an upsurge in respiratory illness among urban populations, while extreme weather events could increase death and injury rates. Water shortages and damaged infrastructure would increase the risk of cholera and dysentery, while higher temperatures would increase the incidence of infectious diseases, such as malaria and dengue fever. Serious social disruption could occur as millions are forced from their homelands as a result of desertification, poor harvests and sea-level rise, while international disputes over shared water resources could turn into conflict.
 G 
 Future climate change could critically undermine efforts for sustainable development in the Mediterranean region through its impacts on the environment and social and economic well-being. While in many respects climate change exacerbates existing problems instead of creating new ones, the sheer magnitude of the potential problem means it cannot be ignored. There is some scope for adaptation, but the fact that many measures would be beneficial irrespective of climate change suggests that radical changes in our policies and practices will be needed. It is also vital that developed countries meet their obligations to assist adaptation in developing countries through access to know-how and financial assistance. Ultimately, however, the long-term sustainability of the Mediterranean region requires keeping climate change within tolerable bounds. Current understanding of safe limits points to the need for prompt international agreement - and action - to make the drastic cuts in emissions of greenhouse gases required to stabilise atmospheric concentrations of these gases.

fields.sentence:
1. Phân tích câu phức (Passage 1 - Đoạn 4): 'Happy people are characterised by the belief that they are able to control their situation, whereas unhappy people tend to believe that they are a victim of fate.'
- Cấu trúc: Câu chứa mệnh đề danh từ ('that they are able...') làm bổ ngữ cho danh từ 'belief'. Liên từ 'whereas' nối hai mệnh đề đối lập giữa 'Happy people' và 'unhappy people'.
- Dịch nghĩa: Những người hạnh phúc được đặc trưng bởi niềm tin rằng họ có khả năng kiểm soát tình huống của mình, trong khi những người không hạnh phúc lại có xu hướng tin rằng họ là nạn nhân của số phận.

2. Phân tích câu phức (Passage 3 - Đoạn B): 'Land degradation occurs all over the world, but it is only referred to as desertification when it takes place in drylands.'
- Cấu trúc: Câu ghép với liên từ 'but' nối hai mệnh đề độc lập. Mệnh đề thứ hai chứa mệnh đề phụ 'when it takes place in drylands' chỉ điều kiện thời gian/địa điểm.
- Dịch nghĩa: Sự suy thoái đất xảy ra trên toàn thế giới, nhưng nó chỉ được gọi là sa mạc hóa khi xảy ra tại các vùng đất khô hạn.
fields.tips:
1. Dạng bài YES/NO/NOT GIVEN: Cần phân biệt rõ: FALSE là thông tin mâu thuẫn trực tiếp; NOT GIVEN là thông tin không được đề cập dù từ khóa có thể xuất hiện. Ví dụ, nếu bài nói 'tiền không mua được hạnh phúc' mà câu hỏi hỏi 'liệu người nghèo có hạnh phúc hơn người giàu', đó là NOT GIVEN.
2. Dạng bài Completion (Summary/Table/Flow-chart): Chú ý từ khóa 'NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS'. Kiểm tra ngữ pháp trong câu tóm tắt để chọn đúng từ loại (danh từ, động từ).
3. Dạng bài Matching Headings: Đọc nhanh câu chủ đề (topic sentence) của mỗi đoạn. Thường tiêu đề chính là ý chính được diễn đạt bằng từ đồng nghĩa (paraphrase). Nếu đoạn văn mang tính liệt kê, tiêu đề thường là danh từ chung.

Task 1:
- Overview: Tất cả các quốc gia đều tăng hoặc giữ nguyên lượng khách. Loại hình du lịch thay đổi từ ưa chuộng backpacking sang resort.
- Body 1: Mô tả biểu đồ cột (tourists): UK và US tăng mạnh (gần gấp đôi), Nhật đạt mốc 1.5 triệu và giữ nguyên.

Task 2:
- Introduction: Dẫn dắt về tầm quan trọng của lãnh đạo. Quan điểm: Năng lực là ưu tiên số 1, không phân biệt tuổi tác.
- Body 1 (Giá trị của người lớn tuổi): Kinh nghiệm quản lý khủng hoảng, mạng lưới quan hệ, sự điềm tĩnh và tầm nhìn dài hạn.
- Body 2 (Giá trị của người trẻ): Sự sáng tạo, am hiểu công nghệ mới, khả năng thích nghi nhanh và tinh thần sẵn sàng đổi mới.

fields.sample:
Task 1:
The provided charts illustrate the number of tourists visiting Australia from three nations (UK, US, and Japan) between 1995 and 2005, alongside trends in travel preferences during the same decade.

Overall, it is evident that visitor numbers from the UK and the US experienced significant growth, while those from Japan remained stable. Furthermore, there was a clear shift in traveler preferences, moving away from backpacking toward resort-based stays by the end of the period.

Regarding tourist numbers, the UK and the US witnessed a remarkable upward trajectory. In 1995, UK visitors stood at 800,000, surging to 1.5 million by 2005. Similarly, US visitor numbers climbed from 500,000 to 1.5 million. In contrast, Japan started at 1.5 million in 1995 and remained at that level in 2005, showing no significant fluctuation.

As for travel types, backpacking was the predominant choice in 1995 and 2000, peaking at approximately 2.4 million participants in 2000 before plummeting to 1.1 million in 2005. Conversely, resort-based travel followed a steady upward trend; it began at a modest 300,000 in 1995, rose to roughly 800,000 in 2000, and finally reached 1.1 million by 2005, matching the popularity of backpacking.


Task 2:
It is a widely held belief that leadership roles in organizations should be reserved for those with extensive experience, who are typically older. Conversely, others argue that younger individuals possess the necessary drive and innovative mindset to lead more effectively. In my opinion, the effectiveness of a leader is not inherently linked to age, and an ideal organizational structure often benefits from the diverse strengths offered by leaders of different generations.

Proponents of older leadership often point to the value of 'institutional wisdom'. Directors and managers who have navigated decades of professional life have likely encountered various market cycles, crises, and organizational challenges. This history allows them to exercise a degree of caution and strategic judgment that is difficult to replicate. Furthermore, senior leaders frequently possess established professional networks and the emotional intelligence required to manage complex stakeholders—attributes that are usually honed over many years of practice.

On the other hand, the argument for younger leadership emphasizes adaptability and innovation. In our rapidly evolving digital economy, younger leaders are often more adept at embracing disruptive technologies and identifying emerging market trends. Their ability to remain agile allows them to steer organizations away from stagnation and toward new opportunities. Moreover, younger managers are often more aligned with the values of the modern workforce, such as prioritizing sustainability, social responsibility, and flexible working environments, which can enhance employee engagement.

However, it is a fallacy to assume that youth guarantees progress or that age guarantees wisdom. The most successful organizations are those that foster a meritocratic environment where leadership is chosen based on competency and vision rather than a birth date. A balanced approach, such as having a younger visionary in a CEO position supported by an experienced board of directors, can create a synergy that combines the caution of age with the dynamism of youth.

In conclusion, I disagree with the view that leadership should be restricted to a specific age group. Whether a leader is young or old is less important than their capability, adaptability, and emotional maturity. Effective organizations should aim to leverage the unique strengths of both generations to achieve sustainable success.

#### **어휘 및 표현 (Từ vựng và biểu hiện)**

**1. 관계가 가장 먼 것을 골라 쓰십시오.**
*(Chọn từ có mối quan hệ xa nhất/khác biệt nhất trong nhóm).*

(1) 기쁘다 (Vui mừng) / 우울하다 (U sầu) / 행복하다 (Hạnh phúc)

---

(2) 만족하다 (Hài lòng) / 떨리다 (Run/Hồi hộp) / 긴장되다 (Căng thẳng)

---

(3) 심심하다 (Buồn chán) / 지루하다 (Nhàm chán) / 불만스럽다 (Bất mãn)

---

(4) 화나다 (Giận dữ) / 무섭다 (Sợ hãi) / 짜증이 나다 (Bực bội)

---

(5) 떨리다 (Run/Hồi hộp) / 슬프다 (Buồn bã) / 괴롭다 (Đau khổ)

---

---

**2. 관계있는 것끼리 연결하십시오.**
*(Hãy nối những cặp có liên quan đến nhau).*

| Cột trái (Nguyên nhân/Tình huống) | Cột phải (Cảm xúc/Trạng thái) |
| --- | --- |
| (1) 할 일이 없다 (Không có việc gì để làm) | ⓐ 화나다 (Giận dữ) |
| (2) 면접 전날이다 (Ngày trước ngày phỏng vấn) | ⓑ 기쁘다 (Vui vẻ) |
| (3) 시험 점수를 생각보다 못 받았다 (Điểm thi thấp hơn mong đợi) | ⓒ 떨리다 (Run/Hồi hộp) |
| (4) 친구가 거짓말을 했다 (Bạn bè nói dối) | ⓓ 심심하다 (Buồn chán) |
| (5) 친한 친구에게서 이메일을 받았다 (Nhận được email từ bạn thân) | ⓔ 불만스럽다 (Bất mãn) |

---

Bạn hãy thử làm bài tập này dựa trên đề bài phía trên nhé! Nếu cần kiểm tra đáp án, bạn cứ cho mình biết.

items.title: đề tiếng hàn bài 5

fields.koreanVocab:
Dưới đây là toàn bộ đề bài và đáp án song ngữ (Hàn - Việt) cho phần bài tập **05 취직 (Xin việc)** trong ảnh mới của bạn:

---

### **05 취직 (05 Xin việc)**

#### **어휘 및 표현 (Từ vựng và biểu hiện)**

---

### **Bài 1: Hãy nhìn các từ dưới đây và chọn từ phù hợp để nối lại (다음 단어를 보고 알맞은 것을 골라 연결하십시오).**

#### **Đề bài & Dịch nghĩa:**

* **(1) 적성에** (Hợp với tính cách/năng lực)
* **(2) 서류를** (Hồ sơ)
* **(3) 자격증을** (Chứng chỉ/Bằng cấp)
* **(4) 필기시험을** (Kỳ thi viết)
* **ⓐ 따다** (Lấy/Đạt được)
* **ⓑ 보다** (Thi/Xem)
* **ⓒ 맞다** (Hợp/Đúng)
* **ⓓ 접수하다** (Nộp/Tiếp nhận)

#### **Đáp án & Dịch nghĩa cụm từ hoàn chỉnh:**

* **(1) - ⓒ : 적성에 맞다** (Hợp với năng khiếu/tính cách)
* **(2) - ⓓ : 서류를 접수하다** (Nộp hồ sơ)
* **(3) - ⓐ : 자격증을 따다** (Lấy chứng chỉ/bằng nghề)
* **(4) - ⓑ : 필기시험을 보다** (Thi viết)

---

### **Bài 2: Hãy tìm từ phù hợp với mô tả dưới đây trong khung `<보기>` và điền vào chỗ trống (다음 설명에 맞는 단어를 <보기>에서 찾아 쓰십시오).**

#### **Từ vựng trong khung `<보기>` (Từ mẫu):**

* **취업** (Xin việc / Đi làm)
* **경력** (Kinh nghiệm làm việc / Lịch sử làm việc)
* **이력서** (Sơ yếu lý lịch)
* **추천서** (Thư giới thiệu)
* **지원 동기** (Động cơ ứng tuyển / Lý do nộp đơn)

#### **Đề bài, Đáp án & Dịch nghĩa:**

**(1) 지금까지 자신이 해 온 업무와 관계있는 일**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Công việc liên quan đến những nhiệm vụ/nghiệp vụ mà bản thân đã làm từ trước cho đến nay.
* **Đáp án:** **경력** (Kinh nghiệm làm việc)

**(2) 어떤 직장이나 조직에 들어가려고 신청한 이유**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Lý do đăng ký để xin vào một nơi làm việc hoặc một tổ chức nào đó.
* **Đáp án:** **지원 동기** (Động cơ ứng tuyển)

**(3) 일정한 일을 구해서 직장에 나가서 돈을 버는 것**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Việc tìm một công việc nhất định, đi làm tại công sở và kiếm tiền.
* **Đáp án:** **취업** (Xin việc)

**(4) 자신의 학력이나 경험한 일 등을 간단하게 쓴 문서**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Tài liệu viết tóm tắt về học vấn hoặc những công việc/kinh nghiệm của bản thân.
* **Đáp án:** **이력서** (Sơ yếu lý lịch)

**(5) 조건에 잘 맞는 사람이나 물건을 다른 사람에게 소개하고 지원하는 글**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Bài viết giới thiệu và hỗ trợ một người hoặc một vật phù hợp với các điều kiện cho người khác.
* **Đáp án:** **추천서** (Thư giới thiệu)
fields.koreanDialogue:
Dưới đây là phần tiếp theo của bài tập (từ câu 2 đến câu 5) được dịch và giải chi tiết theo dạng song ngữ Hàn - Việt:

---

### **Bài 4 (Tiếp theo): Hãy chọn câu trả lời đúng cho đoạn hội thoại dưới đây (다음 대화에 알맞은 것을 고르십시오).**

#### **(2)**

* **A:** 지원서는 어떻게 제출하는지 아세요?
*(Bạn có biết nộp đơn ứng tuyển bằng cách nào không?)*
* **B:** ______________________.
* **ⓐ 졸업 증명서를 내세요** (Hãy nộp bằng tốt nghiệp)
* **ⓑ 이메일로 보내세요** (Hãy gửi qua email)


* **Đáp án:** **ⓑ 이메일로 보내세요**
*(Giải thích: Câu hỏi hỏi về phương thức nộp đơn ứng tuyển (어떻게 제출하는지), nên câu trả lời chỉ cách gửi bằng email là hoàn toàn phù hợp).*

---

#### **(3)**

* **A:** 서류 전형만 통과하면 취직할 수 있나요?
*(Chỉ cần vượt qua vòng hồ sơ là có thể xin được việc đúng không ạ?)*
* **B:** 아니요, ______________________ 취직할 수 있어요.
* **ⓐ 면접시험도 잘 봐야** (Phải thi phỏng vấn tốt nữa mới...)
* **ⓑ 자기소개서를 잘 써야** (Phải viết thư giới thiệu bản thân tốt mới...)


* **Đáp án:** **ⓐ 면접시험도 잘 봐야**
*(Giải thích: "자기소개서" (Thư giới thiệu bản thân) là một phần nằm trong vòng xét duyệt hồ sơ (서류 전형). Vì vậy, sau khi đỗ vòng hồ sơ, ứng viên phải trải qua vòng thi tiếp theo là phỏng vấn (면접시험) thì mới có thể được nhận).*

---

#### **(4)**

* **A:** ______________________?
* **B:** 물론이죠, 작년부터 학원에 다니면서 다 준비해 놓았어요.
*(Dĩ nhiên rồi, tôi đã đi học ở trung tâm từ năm ngoái và chuẩn bị sẵn sàng hết cả rồi).*
* **ⓐ 자격증은 따 놓았어요** (Bạn đã lấy chứng chỉ chưa?)
* **ⓑ 성적 증명서는 준비해 놓았어요** (Bạn đã chuẩn bị bảng điểm chưa?)


* **Đáp án:** **ⓐ 자격증은 따 놓았어요**
*(Giải thích: Việc đi học ở trung tâm/học viện (학원에 다니다) thường hướng tới mục tiêu là thi lấy chứng chỉ/bằng nghề (자격증을 따다) hơn là việc chuẩn bị bảng điểm trường học).*

---

#### **(5)**

* **A:** ______________________?
* **B:** 서류 전형에 통과하면 필기시험과 면접시험이 있습니다.
*(Nếu vượt qua vòng hồ sơ thì sẽ có kỳ thi viết và thi phỏng vấn).*
* **ⓐ 제출 서류는 어떻게 됩니까** (Hồ sơ cần nộp gồm những gì?)
* **ⓑ 전형 방법은 어떻게 됩니까** (Phương thức/Quy trình tuyển chọn như thế nào?)


* **Đáp án:** **ⓑ 전형 방법은 어떻게 됩니까**
*(Giải thích: Câu trả lời của B liệt kê các bước trong quy trình tuyển dụng từ vòng hồ sơ đến thi viết rồi phỏng vấn, do đó câu hỏi phải hỏi về quy trình/phương thức tuyển chọn (전형 방법)).*
fields.koreanPron:
Dưới đây là phần giải nghĩa ngữ pháp và đáp án chi tiết song ngữ (Hàn - Việt) cho trang 53 phần **문법 (Ngữ pháp)** sử dụng cấu trúc **-아/어야** (Phải... thì mới/ chỉ khi... mới):

---

### **Cấu trúc ngữ pháp trọng tâm: -아/어야**

* **Ý nghĩa:** "Phải... thì mới...", "Chỉ khi... thì mới...". Diễn tả hành động hoặc trạng thái ở vế trước là điều kiện bắt buộc, cần thiết để đạt được kết quả ở vế sau.
* **Cách chia:**
* Thân động/tính từ kết thúc bằng nguyên âm **아, 오** + **-아야**
* Thân động/tính từ kết thúc bằng các nguyên âm khác + **-어야**
* Động/tính từ đuôi **하다** chuyển thành **-해야**



---

### **Bài 1: Hãy sử dụng cấu trúc '-아/어야' để hoàn thành câu (1번: ‘-아/어야’를 사용해서 문장을 완성하십시오).**

**(1)** 요즘은 영어를 잘 해야 돼요. 취직을 할 때 외국어 능력을 보는 곳이 많은데 그중에서도 **`영어를 잘해야`** 좋은 점수를 받을 수 있기 때문이에요. *(Gợi ý: 영어를 잘하다)*

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Dạo này phải giỏi tiếng Anh. Khi xin việc có rất nhiều nơi xem xét năng lực ngoại ngữ, mà trong số đó, **phải giỏi tiếng Anh thì mới** nhận được điểm số tốt.

**(2)** 이번 채용은 **`경력이 있어야`** 지원할 수 있어요. 그래서 서류를 낼 때 경력증명서도 함께 내야 해요. *(Gợi ý: 경력이 있다)*

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Đợt tuyển dụng lần này **phải có kinh nghiệm thì mới** có thể ứng tuyển. Vì thế khi nộp hồ sơ, bạn phải nộp kèm cả giấy chứng nhận kinh nghiệm làm việc.

**(3)** 예전에는 채용 공고문을 학교 게시판에서 봤는데 이제는 **`학교 홈페이지에 들어가야`** 확인할 수 있어요. 그래서 매일 학교 홈페이지에 들어가요. *(Gợi ý: 학교 홈페이지에 들어가다)*

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Ngày trước tôi thường xem thông báo tuyển dụng trên bảng tin của trường, nhưng bây giờ **phải vào trang web của trường thì mới** kiểm tra được. Vì vậy, ngày nào tôi cũng truy cập vào trang web của trường.

**(4)** 외국어는 **`말하기 연습을 열심히 해야`** 빨리 잘 할 수 있어요. 말하기 연습을 열심히 하지 않으면 금방 잊어버리니까 시간이 있을 때마다 연습하세요. *(Gợi ý: 말하기 연습을 열심히 하다)*

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Đối với ngoại ngữ, **phải luyện nói thật chăm chỉ thì mới** nhanh giỏi được. Nếu không luyện nói chăm chỉ thì sẽ quên ngay thôi, nên bất cứ khi nào có thời gian bạn hãy luyện tập nhé.

**(5)** 직장을 선택할 때는 자기의 적성을 잘 생각해야 해요. **`적성에 맞아야`** 직장 생활을 잘 할 수 있어요. *(Gợi ý: 적성에 맞다)*

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Khi lựa chọn nơi làm việc, bạn phải suy nghĩ kỹ về năng khiếu của bản thân. **Phải hợp với năng khiếu/tính cách thì mới** có thể thích nghi tốt với cuộc sống công sở.

---

### **Bài 2: Hãy sử dụng cấu trúc '-아/어야' để hoàn thành hội thoại (2번: ‘-아/어야’를 사용해서 대화를 완성하십시오).**

**(1)**

* **A:** 여권을 잃어버렸는데 여행갈 수 있을까요?
*(Tôi bị mất hộ chiếu rồi, liệu có đi du lịch được không nhỉ?)*
* **B:** **`여권을 다시 만들어야 (또는 여권이 있어야)`** 해외 여행을 갈 수 있지요. 빨리 준비해 놓으세요.
*(**Phải làm lại hộ chiếu (hoặc: Phải có hộ chiếu) thì mới** đi du lịch nước ngoài được chứ. Mau chuẩn bị đi nhé).*

**(2)**

* **A:** 한국 친구를 꼭 사귀어야 해요?
*(Có nhất thiết phải kết bạn với người Hàn Quốc không?)*
* **B:** 물론이죠. **`한국 친구를 사귀어야`** 한국어 연습을 많이 할 수 있어요.
*(Tất nhiên rồi. **Phải kết bạn với người Hàn Quốc thì mới** có thể luyện tập tiếng Hàn nhiều được).*
fields.koreanTranslation:
Dưới đây là phần dịch và giải đáp án chi tiết song ngữ cho hai phần bài tập trong ảnh của bạn:

---

### **Phần 1: Tiếp tục với cấu trúc -아/어야 (Phải... thì mới...)**

**(3)**

* **A:** **`졸업 시험에 통과해야`** 졸업을 할 수 있지요?
*(**Phải vượt qua kỳ thi tốt nghiệp** thì mới được tốt nghiệp đúng không ạ?)*
* **B:** 네, 그러니까 이번 졸업 시험에 꼭 통과하세요.
*(Đúng vậy, thế nên lần này nhất định phải thi đỗ kỳ thi tốt nghiệp đấy nhé).*

**(4)**

* **A:** 지원서는 이메일 대신에 우편으로 보낼 거예요.
*(Tôi định gửi đơn ứng tuyển bằng bưu điện thay vì email).*
* **B:** 안 돼요. 너무 늦어서 **`이메일로 보내야`** 마감 시간을 지킬 수 있어요.
*(Không được đâu. Muộn lắm rồi, **phải gửi bằng email thì mới** kịp hạn chót đấy).*

**(5)**

* **A:** 아직 대학교를 졸업하지 못했는데 그 회사에 지원할 수 있을까요?
*(Tôi vẫn chưa tốt nghiệp đại học, liệu có ứng tuyển vào công ty đó được không ạ?)*
* **B:** **`대학교를 졸업해야`** 지원할 수 있으니까 다른 회사를 알아보고세요.
*(**Phải tốt nghiệp đại học thì mới** ứng tuyển được, nên bạn hãy tìm kiếm công ty khác xem sao).*

---

### **Phần 2: Cấu trúc ngữ pháp mới: -아/어 놓다 (Làm sẵn / Làm sẵn để duy trì trạng thái)**

* **Ý nghĩa:** Diễn tả hành động nào đó đã được hoàn thành và trạng thái hoặc kết quả của hành động đó vẫn được duy trì nguyên vẹn cho đến hiện tại (thường dịch là **"làm sẵn...", "làm trước..."**).
* **Cách chia:** Chia động từ ở dạng **-아/어** rồi kết hợp với **놓다**.

#### **Từ vựng trong khung `<보기>` (Từ mẫu):**

* **쌓다**: Tích lũy, chồng chất
* **찾다**: Tìm kiếm, rút (tiền)
* **쓰다**: Viết
* **꺼내다**: Lấy ra, rút ra
* **만들다**: Làm, tạo ra
* **신청하다**: Đăng ký

#### **Đề bài, Đáp án & Dịch nghĩa:**

**(1) 책을 이렇게 `쌓아 놓지` 말고 책장에 꽂아서 정리를 하세요.**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Đừng **xếp chồng** sách lên như thế này nữa, hãy cắm vào giá sách và thu dọn đi.
* *Giải thích:* Động từ **쌓다** (chồng chất) + **-아 놓다** $\rightarrow$ **쌓아 놓다** (chồng sẵn lên). Trong câu có cấu trúc phủ định **-지 말고** (đừng làm vế trước mà hãy làm vế sau) nên chia là **쌓아 놓지 말고**.

**(2) 물건을 계산할 때 필요한 돈을 지갑에서 미리 `꺼내 놓으면` 오래 기다리지 않아서 좋아요.**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Khi thanh toán đồ dùng, nếu **lấy sẵn** số tiền cần thiết ra khỏi ví từ trước thì sẽ rất tiện vì không phải chờ đợi lâu.
* *Giải thích:* Động từ **꺼내다** (lấy ra) + **-어 놓다** $\rightarrow$ **꺼내 놓다** (lấy sẵn ra). Kết hợp với giả thuyết **-(으)면** $\rightarrow$ **꺼내 놓으면**.

**(3) 다음 달에 보는 영어시험은 이번 주까지 `신청해 놓아야` 돼요. 그렇지 않으면 6개월 동안 기다려야 돼요.**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Kỳ thi tiếng Anh diễn ra vào tháng sau thì **phải đăng ký sẵn** trước tuần này mới được. Nếu không thì sẽ phải đợi tận 6 tháng đấy.
* *Giải thích:* Động từ **신청하다** (đăng ký) + **-어 놓다** $\rightarrow$ **신청해 놓다** (đăng ký sẵn). Kết hợp với cấu trúc bắt buộc **-아야/어야 하다/되다** $\rightarrow$ **신청해 놓아야 돼요**.

**(4) 자기소개서를 미리 `써 놓으면` 입사 서류를 낼 때 준비하는 시간을 줄일 수 있어서 좀 더 편할 거예요.**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Nếu **viết sẵn** trước thư giới thiệu bản thân thì khi nộp hồ sơ xin việc sẽ giảm bớt được thời gian chuẩn bị, như vậy sẽ thoải mái hơn một chút.
* *Giải thích:* Động từ **쓰다** (viết) + **-어 놓다** $\rightarrow$ **써 놓다** (viết sẵn). Kết hợp với giả thuyết **-(으)면** $\rightarrow$ **써 놓으면**.

**(5) 이번 업무에 필요한 자료는 다 찾았어요? 그 자료를 오늘 다 `찾아 놓아야` 이번 주까지 일을 끝낼 수 있어요.**

* *Dịch nghĩa:* Bạn đã tìm hết các tài liệu cần thiết cho công việc lần này chưa? Hôm nay **phải tìm sẵn** hết đống tài liệu đó ra thì mới có thể hoàn thành công việc trước tuần này được.
* *Giải thích:* Động từ **찾다** (tìm kiếm) + **-아 놓다** $\rightarrow$ **찾아 놓다** (tìm sẵn). Kết hợp với ngữ pháp chỉ điều kiện cần **-아야/어야** $\rightarrow$ **찾아 놓아야** (hoặc **찾아 놓아야 해요/돼요**).

---

Bạn có cần mình giải thích kỹ hơn về các bước biến đổi đuôi câu hay ngữ pháp nào khác trong bài này không?

fields.sample:
Task 1:
The provided charts illustrate the number of tourists visiting Australia from three nations (UK, US, and Japan) between 1995 and 2005, alongside trends in travel preferences during the same decade.

Overall, it is clear that visitor numbers from the UK and the US experienced significant growth, while those from Japan remained stable. Furthermore, there was a clear shift in traveler preferences, moving away from backpacking toward resort-based stays by the end of the period.

Regarding tourist numbers, the UK and the US witnessed a remarkable upward trajectory. In 1995, UK visitors stood at 800,000, surging to 1.5 million by 2005. Similarly, US visitor numbers climbed from 500,000 to 1.5 million. In contrast, Japan started at 1.5 million in 1995 and remained at that level in 2005, showing no significant fluctuation.

As for travel types, backpacking was the predominant choice in 1995 and 2000, peaking at approximately 2.4 million participants in 2000 before plummeting to 1.1 million in 2005. Conversely, resort-based travel followed a steady upward trend; it began at a modest 300,000 in 1995, rose to roughly 800,000 in 2000, and finally reached 1.1 million by 2005, nearly matching the popularity of backpacking by the end of the timeframe.


Task 2:
It is a widely held belief that leadership roles in organizations should be reserved for those with extensive experience, who are typically older. Conversely, others argue that younger individuals possess the necessary drive and innovative mindset to lead more effectively. In my opinion, the effectiveness of a leader is not inherently linked to age, and an ideal organizational structure often benefits from the diverse strengths offered by leaders of different generations.

On the one hand, older managers are often favored for their deep institutional knowledge and seasoned judgment. Leadership is not merely about making quick decisions; it is about steering an organization through cycles of economic uncertainty, which requires the perspective gained only through years of professional practice. These leaders have often encountered a multitude of market failures and successes, providing them with a 'war-chest' of experience that allows them to remain calm under pressure. Their professional networks are typically extensive, which can be an invaluable asset for an organization looking to form strategic partnerships.

On the other hand, the argument for younger leadership emphasizes adaptability and innovation. In our rapidly evolving digital economy, younger leaders are often more adept at embracing disruptive technologies and identifying emerging market trends. Their ability to remain agile allows them to steer organizations away from stagnation and toward new opportunities. Moreover, younger managers are often more aligned with the values of the modern workforce, such as prioritizing sustainability and flexible working environments, which can enhance employee engagement.

However, it is a fallacy to assume that youth guarantees competence just as it is to assume age guarantees wisdom. The most successful organizations are those that foster a meritocratic environment where leadership is chosen based on competency and vision rather than a birth date. A balanced approach, such as having a younger visionary in a CEO position supported by an experienced board of directors, can create a synergy that combines the caution of age with the dynamism of youth.

In conclusion, I disagree with the view that leadership should be restricted to a specific age group. Whether a leader is young or old is less important than their capability, adaptability, and emotional maturity. Effective organizations should aim to leverage the unique strengths of both generations to achieve sustainable success.

Task 1:
- Dạng biểu đồ: Biểu đồ tròn (Pie charts) so sánh sự thay đổi về tỷ lệ độ tuổi du khách từ năm 1983 đến 2003.

- Phân tích: Nhóm 35-54 là nhóm lớn nhất nhưng giảm tỷ lệ. Nhóm 55+ và 16-24 tăng mạnh nhất. Nhóm 0-15 và 25-34 biến động nhẹ.

- Hướng dẫn: Phân tích trách nhiệm của cả nhà sản xuất (giảm bao bì tại nguồn) và người tiêu dùng (từ chối mua hàng đóng gói dư thừa). Quan điểm: Cả hai bên đều cần phối hợp.
fields.ideas:
Task 1:
- Overview: Cơ cấu độ tuổi du khách thay đổi rõ rệt; nhóm 35-54 giảm vị thế thống trị, trong khi nhóm trẻ (16-24) và già (55+) trở nên phổ biến hơn.
- Body 1: Mô tả nhóm giảm hoặc giữ nguyên: Nhóm 35-54 (giảm 50% -> 35%), nhóm 25-34 (giảm 20% -> 12%).
- Body 2: Mô tả nhóm tăng: Nhóm 55+ (tăng 16% -> 26%), nhóm 16-24 (tăng 4% -> 15%), nhóm 0-15 (tăng 10% -> 12%).

Task 2:
- Introduction: Đặt vấn đề về vấn đề rác thải bao bì hiện nay. Lập trường: Trách nhiệm thuộc về cả hai phía, doanh nghiệp đóng vai trò chủ chốt, người tiêu dùng đóng vai trò thúc đẩy.
- Body 1 (Trách nhiệm doanh nghiệp): Sản xuất sạch, thiết kế bao bì bền vững, dùng vật liệu tái chế. Họ có quyền lực kinh tế để thay đổi quy trình.
- Body 2 (Trách nhiệm người tiêu dùng): Lựa chọn sản phẩm không đóng gói quá mức, ép buộc doanh nghiệp thay đổi thông qua sức mua (voting with wallets).
- Conclusion: Phối hợp là chìa khóa. Chính phủ cần hỗ trợ bằng luật pháp.
fields.sample:
Task 1:
The two pie charts compare the age distribution of tourists traveling from the UK to Spain in 1983 and 2003, highlighting significant shifts in the demographics of visitors over the two-decade period.

Overall, the most prominent feature is the decline in the dominance of the 35-54 age group, which was the largest segment in 1983, and a notable rise in the popularity of Spain among both the youngest and oldest travelers by 2003.

In 1983, the 35-54 age group accounted for exactly half of all visitors, at 50%. However, this figure dropped to 35% twenty years later. Similarly, the percentage of travelers aged 25-34 fell from 20% to 12% over the same duration. 

In contrast, other age brackets experienced growth. The oldest segment, those aged 55 and above, saw their share increase from 16% to 26%, becoming the second-largest group in 2003. Even more dramatic was the surge in the 16-24 age group, which nearly quadrupled from 4% to 15%. Finally, the youngest cohort, aged 0-15, also grew, albeit more modestly, from 10% to 12%. In summary, while the middle-aged segments became less prevalent, Spain saw a younger and older demographic composition among UK visitors in 2003 compared to 1983.


Task 2:
The issue of excessive packaging in retail products is a growing environmental concern. While some argue that the onus for waste reduction lies solely with the manufacturers and supermarkets, others contend that consumers hold the power to dictate market trends through their buying habits. In my opinion, this problem requires a concerted effort from both parties, though corporations must take the leading role in driving sustainable solutions.

Those who believe that the responsibility rests with producers and retailers argue that they have the systemic power to alter manufacturing processes. Supermarkets and manufacturers control the materials and designs used for packaging. By implementing 'circular economy' models—such as using biodegradable materials, reducing plastic film, and promoting bulk-buy stations—they can drastically reduce the volume of waste at the source. It is unfair to expect consumers to make perfect ethical choices when many products are simply not available in sustainable packaging. Therefore, government regulation should hold these corporations accountable for the lifecycle of their packaging.

Conversely, those who advocate for consumer responsibility believe that 'voting with one’s wallet' is the most effective way to spark change. If individuals consistently refuse to purchase goods wrapped in unnecessary layers of plastic, supermarkets will be forced to adapt their inventory to survive in a competitive market. Furthermore, consumers can significantly reduce waste by choosing locally sourced, unpackaged produce. By actively seeking out eco-friendly alternatives, consumers send a clear signal that sustainability is a non-negotiable preference, thereby compelling manufacturers to innovate.

However, in my view, assigning sole responsibility to one party ignores the complexity of modern consumerism. Many low-income families are constrained by price and accessibility, meaning they may not have the luxury to choose 'green' options even if they want to. Consequently, manufacturers must make sustainable packaging the standard, not a premium 'choice' for the wealthy. Retailers should facilitate this by redesigning their shelves and supply chains to reward low-waste products.

In conclusion, while consumers play a vital role in influencing the market, the primary responsibility for reducing packaging lies with the companies that produce it. A truly sustainable solution will only emerge when governments, producers, and individuals act in concert, with corporations spearheading the shift toward less wasteful practices.

 Other options (bus, train) aren’t mentioned—only “drop him off by car.” Focus on what is done, not alternative possibilities.

 Questions 11-13 Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 
 Resilience 

 11
 According to the speaker, parents are reluctant to let their children play outside because

 A the crime rate is increasing. 
 B children cannot assess danger properly. 
 C it is harder for children to socialise outside. 
 Answer: A Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 The audioscript states that fear of crime prevents parents from letting children play outside.
"One of the main reasons why parents are reluctant to let their children play outside is fear of crime. They worry that their children might be abducted or harmed..."

 12
 Research shows that playgrounds have been made safer because of

 A increased insurance claims. 
 B pressure from the media. 
 C changes in the law. 
 Answer: A Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 The audioscript mentions playgrounds becoming safer due to compensation claims for injuries.
"...this has been done in response to claims for compensation when children have been injured."

 13
 According to the speaker, children best learn to handle bullies by

 A talking to their parents. 
 B staying home. 
 C playing with other children. 
 Answer: C Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 By playing with other children because the speaker explicitly states that children
"need to be able to develop their own strategies for coping with bullies, and they can only do that if they are allowed to play with other children." So the answer is C.

 Questions 14-15 Choose TWO letters, A–E .
 What TWO things parents can do to help children develop resilience?

 A give them tasks to do on their own. 
 B go shopping with them. 
 C reassure them when necessary. 
 D help children avoid injuries. 
 E encourage children to do better. 
 14-15 Answer: A,C Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 The script states: "Parents can also encourage children to be more independent. For example, they could let them walk to school by themselves, or go to the shops on their own." Giving them tasks to do on their own (like walking to school or going to the shops) directly aligns with encouraging independence, which is presented as a way to develop resilience. So the answer is A.
The script says: "If a child falls over and gets a cut on his leg, for example, the parent can help by staying calm and reassuring the child that it’s only a small cut and it will soon get better." Reassuring the child in moments of minor distress is explicitly mentioned as a way for parents to help. So the answer is C.

 Questions 16-17 Choose TWO letters, A–E .
 What TWO things parents can do to help children learn about risks?

 A limit the risks they are exposed to. 
 B encourage them to talk about risks. 
 C have discussions with the children’s friends. 
 D do indoor activities. 
 E try not to influence their actions. 
 16-17 Answer: B,E Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 The script says parents should help by "asking questions like, 'How high do you think you can climb?' and 'What’s the worst thing that could happen if you fall?'" This is a direct example of encouraging them to talk about or discuss the risks. So, B is correct.
The script explicitly states parents should "encourage them to think about the risks... and to decide for themselves whether or not they want to take those risks." This aligns with "try not to influence their actions" in the sense of letting the child decide. So, E is correct.

 - Children can join a 18 team and try a new hobby.
 - Children should learn how to take risks in a 19 environment.

 The phrase "join a sports team" directly fills the blank. "Sport" is also acceptable as it refers to the type of team.

 19 Answer: controlled Nghe từ đây Locate Giải thích Report 
 The audio script explicitly states: "...These activities will help children to develop confidence and learn how to take risks in a controlled environment." The phrase "controlled environment" is a direct quote from the audio, perfectly fitting the blank in the sentence. 

 20 Answer: independent Nghe từ đây Giải thích Report 
 The question's blank asks for a quality that children become "more ____ and confident." The audio directly links "confident" with "independent" as outcomes of these parenting strategies. Therefore, "independent" is the word from the script that logically completes the sentence

 PART 1 Receptionist: Good morning, Sunridge Summer Camp. This is Anna speaking. How may I assist you?
 Parent: Hi there! I’m calling to register my son for your summer program. I saw the two-week camp on your website and thought it’d be a great experience for him.
 Receptionist: Lovely. I’ll just take a few details to get things started. What’s your son’s name, please?
 Parent: His name is Lucas Turner.
 Receptionist: Thanks. Now, could you tell me his age?
 Parent: He just turned 13 last month, but the website says the age range is 9 to 12. Is that a problem?
 Receptionist: Actually, 13 is just outside the regular range, but if he turned 13 recently, we can still accept him. So I’ll put down 12 years old. 
 Receptionist: And which session would you like him to attend?
 Parent: We were looking at the one starting July 3rd, running for two weeks.
 Receptionist: So, from July 3rd to 17th , correct?
 Parent: Yes, that’s right.
 Receptionist: Can I have your home address for our records?
 Parent: Sure, it’s 21 Maple Grove, Ashbury. That’s A-s-h-b-u-r-y.
 Receptionist: Maple Grove... Ashbury . Got it.
 Receptionist: And what’s the best phone number to reach you?
 Parent: Um, my mobile is 7984 657 392. Or we have a home number too—wait, never mind, the mobile’s better. 
 Receptionist: Any medical or dietary issues we should be aware of?
 Parent: He’s vegetarian, but that’s more of a preference. The only real concern is his peanut allergy. It’s not extremely severe, but we do carry an EpiPen just in case. 
 Receptionist: Duly noted. Now, we offer a range of activities—are there any that Lucas is particularly interested in?
 Parent: Oh, he loves all kinds of outdoor stuff. He’s not really into crafts or drama, but he’s especially keen on swimming and archery. 
 Receptionist: We’ve got both of those!
 —--------------------
 Receptionist: Has he attended an overnight camp before?
 Parent: No, he hasn’t. He’s done day camps back home in York, but this will be his first time staying away from home overnight. 
 Receptionist: Thanks, we’ll make sure he’s placed in a beginner group.
 Receptionist: Will Lucas bring his own sleeping bag?
 Parent: Hmm, I thought he had one, but it turns out it’s too small. So we’ll need to borrow one from the camp, if that’s possible.
 Receptionist: Absolutely, we have spares for hire. There’s a small charge, which I’ll include in the invoice.
 Receptionist: And how will Lucas get to the camp?
 Parent: Originally, we were going to send him by coach, but since we’ll be in the area anyway, we’ve decided to drop him off by car on the morning of the 3rd. 
 Receptionist: All right. Lastly, how would you like to handle payment?
 Parent: Hmm, I’d rather not give card details over the phone. Do you take cheques?
 Receptionist: We no longer accept cheques, I’m afraid, but you can pay online through our website. It’s very secure.
 Parent: That works. I’ll do that later today.
 Receptionist: Perfect! Once payment is made, you’ll receive a confirmation email with all the details. Let us know if anything changes.
 Parent: Will do. Thanks for all your help!

 PART 2 Today, I’m going to talk about the issue of encouraging children to learn about risk. At the moment, a lot of children are not allowed to play outside by themselves, so, unsurprisingly, there are concerns about how this is affecting them.
 One of the main reasons why parents are reluctant to let their children play outside is fear of crime. They worry that their children might be abducted or harmed in some way by a stranger. But research shows that the chances of a child being abducted are very low. In fact, they are far more likely to be injured in a car accident than to be abducted. There are also concerns about the risk of accidents. In recent years, playgrounds have been made much safer than they were in the past, and this has been done in response to claims for compensation when children have been injured. But this has had an unexpected result. While children can still have accidents in playgrounds, they are less likely to be injured than they were in the past. But, in fact, they are more likely to have accidents elsewhere, because they have had fewer opportunities to learn how to take risks.
 Another concern is about the risk of bullying. Parents worry that their children will be hurt by other children. But, again, if children are kept at home, they won’t learn how to deal with bullies. They need to be able to develop their own strategies for coping with bullies, and they can only do that if they are allowed to play with other children. 
 So, what can parents do to help children to develop resilience?
 One thing that parents can do is to avoid overreacting to minor injuries. If a child falls over and gets a cut on his leg, for example, the parent can help by staying calm and reassuring the child that it’s only a small cut and it will soon get better. Parents can also encourage children to be more independent. For example, they could let them walk to school by themselves, or go to the shops on their own. This will help them to develop confidence and learn how to take responsibility for themselves. 
 —
 It’s also important for children to learn how to manage risks. Parents can help by encouraging them to think about the risks involved in different activities and to decide for themselves whether or not they want to take those risks. For example, if a child wants to climb a tree, the parent can help by asking questions like, “How high do you think you can climb?” and “What’s the worst thing that could happen if you fall?” This will help the child to think about the risks involved and to make an informed decision.
 Another way that parents can help is by encouraging children to solve their own problems. For example, if a child is having trouble with a friend, the parent can help by asking questions like, “What do you think you could do to make things better?” and “How do you think your friend feels about the situation?” This will help the child to think about the problem from different angles and to come up with a solution. 
 Finally, parents can help by encouraging children to take part in activities that involve a certain amount of risk. For example, they could encourage them to join a sports team or to take up a hobby like rock climbing or skiing. These activities will help children to develop confidence and learn how to take risks in a controlled environment. 
 So, in conclusion, it’s important for children to learn about risk, and parents can help by encouraging them to be more independent, to manage risks, to solve their own problems, and to take part in activities that involve a certain amount of risk. By doing this, they will help their children to develop resilience and to become more confident and independent adults.

 PART 3 Emma: Hi, Jack. How was your weekend?
 Jack: Oh, great, thanks, Emma. I actually went cycling again. To be honest, I'm getting a bit obsessed with it.
 Emma: Oh, I remember you mentioned thinking about buying a bike. Did you get one then?
 Jack: Yes, I did! I bought a really nice one. I was looking at a few different types, but I ended up getting a mountain bike. I figured I'd be able to ride it in more places than a road bike. 
 Emma: That's true, isn't it? So, where did you go?
 Jack: I went to the forest. There are some excellent paths there that are just right for mountain biking. It's really good exercise, and it's great to be out in the fresh air instead of at the gym, you know?
 Emma: I know exactly what you mean. I'd like to try cycling, but I'm not sure it's for me. I think I'd be a bit scared of riding on the roads. 
 Jack: Well, I was too, but it's fine once you get used to it. You really should try it. It's a fantastic way to keep fit, and you can explore so many different places. I've been all over the city on my bike.
 Emma: I've heard cycling is incredibly beneficial. It's better than running because it doesn't put stress on your joints. 
 Jack: Exactly! And it's better than driving because you don't have to sit in traffic jams. It's a lot quicker than walking, and you can reach places you can't get to on public transport.
 Emma: And it's good for the environment too, isn't it?
 Jack: Yes, it's very environmentally friendly. So, why don't you give it a go? You can borrow my bike if you like. 
 Emma: I might just do that, thanks. I'll let you know.
 Jack: I honestly think more people should cycle. It would be good for the country's health overall.
 Emma: That's very true. I read somewhere that people who cycle to work are fitter and healthier than those who don't.
 Jack: Yes, I read that too. I think the government should definitely encourage more people to cycle instead of driving.
 …………………………..
 Emma: I think they do, actually. I read that some local councils have been building cycle lanes to encourage people to ride their bikes. 
 Jack: Yes, that's right. I've been on some of those new cycle lanes myself.
 Emma: And some companies are encouraging their employees to cycle to work. They're giving them free bikes or paying for bike repairs, that sort of thing.
 Jack: Yes, I've heard about that. And some local councils are even offering free cycling lessons to help people who are nervous about riding on the roads. 
 Emma: Good idea. I think I'd definitely need some lessons!
 Jack: And there are also cycle clubs that organise group rides. I've been on a couple of those. It's a really good way to meet people.
 Emma: Yes, I can imagine. It's probably more fun than cycling on your own, I suppose.
 Jack: Yes, it is. And you feel a lot safer when you're in a group. 
 Emma: I think I'd be afraid of breathing in all the fumes from the traffic, though.
 Jack: Yes, that is a problem, unfortunately. According to a recent report, vehicle emissions are the main cause of air pollution in cities, and that's a big concern for cyclists. I've started wearing a mask when I cycle in the city. It's not very comfortable, but I think it helps.
 Emma: I've seen people wearing those masks. They look quite strange, but I suppose it's better than breathing in all those dangerous fumes.
 Jack: Yes, I think so. And another problem is that the roads are in such bad condition in some places. There are so many potholes, and some roads are so uneven. It's quite dangerous sometimes. 
 Emma: Yes, I've heard that. I think it's really important to wear a helmet to protect your head if you fall off your bike.
 Jack: Yes, I always wear a helmet, and I wear bright clothing so that drivers can see me. I think that's absolutely crucial.
 Emma: Yes, I agree. So, where are you going to cycle next weekend?
 Jack: I'm not sure, actually. I might go to the forest again, or I might try somewhere new. I'd really like to find a group of cyclists to go with.
 Emma: Yes, you should definitely do that. I'll have a look online to see if there are any groups in this area.
 Jack: Good idea. I'll do that too.

 PART 4 Good morning, everyone. In this final week of our series on the history of film, we’ll be exploring the rise of colour and sound in cinema, focusing on a key period known as the Golden Age of Hollywood, which lasted from around 1917 to the end of the 1930s.
 This era truly began in 1917 with the development of silent films. A major early example was The Birth of a Nation, directed by D.W. Griffith. It was a huge success at the time, though now it's widely criticised for its offensive and racist content. During this silent film period, movies were shown in black and white and relied on written captions to show dialogue. Live music—often played by a pianist or small orchestra—helped add emotion and atmosphere. Because there was no spoken dialogue, actors had to rely on dramatic facial expressions and exaggerated movements to tell the story. 
 As the popularity of cinema grew, several major studios were founded in Hollywood. This transformed the small California town into the centre of the film world. Stars like Charlie Chaplin, famous for his comic roles , and Mary Pickford, known as “America’s Sweetheart,” became international icons. These actors helped draw massive audiences, and the studios quickly became powerful businesses. Major companies like Paramount, MGM, and Warner Bros. controlled nearly every part of the film process—from hiring actors to showing films in their own cinemas. This structure became known as the “studio system.” 
 A major turning point came in 1927 with the release of The Jazz Singer. This was the first successful film to include synchronised sound and spoken dialogue. It marked the beginning of a new era: “the talkies.” The impact was enormous. Audiences were amazed, and soon all major studios began producing sound films. However, the shift wasn’t easy. Some silent film stars struggled to adapt because their voices didn’t suit the new technology, or their acting style didn’t work with spoken dialogue. Studios also had to invest large sums of money in new recording equipment and redesign their sets to prevent sound problems.
 Despite the economic difficulties of the 1930s, including the Great Depression, Hollywood continued to produce a wide variety of films. People had less money, but they still went to the cinema to escape from daily life. Studios made musicals, romantic comedies, action films, and dramas—many of which are still popular today. These films gave audiences hope, glamour, and fantasy in difficult times.
 The 1930s also brought new technology, particularly in colour. While colour films had existed in some form for years, the process was expensive and difficult. That began to change with the introduction of Technicolor, which allowed for brighter, more stable colours. A major breakthrough came in 1937 with Walt Disney’s Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first full-length animated feature. It was a huge success and showed that animation could be both artistically impressive and commercially viable.
 By 1939, several important films were released that are now considered classics, such as Gone with the Wind and The Wizard of Oz. Both were made in colour and are often seen as the peak of Hollywood’s Golden Age . But 1939 also marked the beginning of World War II, which had a major effect on the film industry. Many actors and directors joined the war effort, and studios began making propaganda films to support national morale. After the war, the industry faced new challenges.
 One of these was the rise of television in the 1950s. For the first time, people could be entertained at home for free, which led to a drop in cinema attendance. In response, studios tried to bring audiences back with new innovations like widescreen formats and 3D films. Although these methods had mixed success, they showed how the film industry had to keep evolving to stay relevant.
 While the Golden Age technically ended in the 1940s, its influence continues to shape modern cinema. The foundations built during those early decades—from storytelling techniques to studio production—still affect how movies are made today.
 So, in summary, the early 20th century was a time of dramatic change in film. From silent black-and-white movies to full-colour sound films, the industry grew rapidly in both technology and storytelling. It adapted to new challenges and found ways to continue entertaining audiences around the world. Next week, we’ll look at the rise of independent cinema and how filmmakers outside the big studios began to reshape the industry.
